scc.gui.quarry.cards.tip: Void, Silk Touch, Fortune (level %s on this tier), Ores Only, Fluids, Fill Holes, Orbital Mining. Each card costs extra FE per block. This tier opens %s of %s slots.
scc.gui.quarry.f.0.tip: Size of the area across, seen from the front of the core.
scc.gui.quarry.f.1.tip: Size of the area away from the core - it lies behind the core; the front faces you when you place it.
scc.gui.quarry.f.2.tip: How many layers down from the top layer.
scc.gui.quarry.f.3.tip: Where the area starts: blocks behind the core (negative: in front of it).
scc.gui.quarry.f.4.tip: Shift to the right, seen from the front of the core (negative: to the left).
scc.gui.quarry.f.5.tip: Top layer relative to the core (0: the core's own height, -1: the layer below it).
scc.gui.quarry.fill.tip: Click with a full block in your hand (or drag one in from JEI/EMI). Right-click with an empty hand: back to cobblestone. Taken from the network, otherwise from the buffer.
scc.gui.quarry.fluids.tip: Water and lava source blocks in the area are replaced with the fill block while mining - no lava lakes, no floods. Fluids running in from outside are sealed off too. With the Fluids card the source is pumped into the network first.
scc.gui.quarry.info.orbital: Orbital: %s hauls · %s FE each · every %s s
scc.gui.quarry.info.orbital.loot: Orbital: %s hauls · tier loot table · every %s s
scc.gui.quarry.info.orbital.ores: Orbital: %s hauls · %s ore kinds here · every %s s
scc.gui.quarry.info.power: %s FE/block · %s FE/t at full speed · buffer %s
scc.gui.quarry.info.power.orbital: %s FE per haul · %s FE/t on average · %s FE stored
scc.gui.quarry.map.tip: The area from above, north is up. Darker means deeper; the gold dot is the core, the blinking square the spot being mined.
scc.gui.quarry.markers.tip: Takes the area from Quarry Markers: one within 3 blocks of the core, one each along X and Z at the same height. The top layer is the markers' height - they are mined too and land in storage.
scc.gui.quarry.maxheight: Height: up to %s above the core (build limit)
scc.gui.quarry.power.rate: Full speed: %s FE/t (%s FE per block before hardness)
scc.gui.quarry.power.tip: Hard blocks cost more, air and filtered blocks nothing. If the network delivers less, the quarry mines slower and shows Not enough power.
scc.gui.quarry.refill.tip: After mining, the quarry fills the pit again from the bottom up with the fill block from the network. Only the spots it dug out (and caves below them) - never the open air above the old ground. A quarter of the mining price per block. Done means mined and filled.
scc.gui.quarry.restart.tip: Starts again at the top layer - mined spots are air and are skipped for free.
scc.gui.quarry.run.tip: Starts or pauses mining. A redstone signal pauses it too.
scc.gui.quarry.scan.tip: Counts the ores in the area again (loaded chunks only).
scc.gui.quarry.st.idle: Ready - set the area and press Start
scc.gui.quarry.st.loading: Loading the chunk it mines next ...
scc.gui.quarry.st.protected: Protected - the claim does not allow it
scc.gui.quarry.st.settling: Picking up gravel and sand that slid in
scc.gui.quarry.st.unloaded: Waiting - part of the area is not loaded
scc.gui.quarry.step: Click ±1, Shift ±16, Ctrl ±64, Ctrl+Shift ±256 - the mouse wheel works too. Click the number to type a value (Tab: next field).
scc.gui.quarry.survey.size: Tier: %s per side - with a survey tool up to %s
scc.gui.quarry.survey.tip: Put a Quarry Survey Tool linked to this quarry here: its area is applied at once, and while it sits here the area may be bigger than the tier allows.
scc.gui.quarry.title: Star Quarry
scc.gui.recent.empty: Nothing ordered yet. Every order you place from a terminal shows up here - per player, kept across restarts.
scc.gui.recent.help: Click: fill in - Shift: order now - Right: remove
scc.gui.recent.open.tip: Your last 10 orders with amount. Click opens the order window filled in, Shift + click orders again right away.
scc.gui.recent.shift: Click: order window with this amount - Shift + click: order again now
scc.gui.recent.title: Recently ordered
scc.gui.reciperules.add.tip: Pick an item, then set the order of its recipe types and which ones are never used.
scc.gui.reciperules.applies: A network recipe rule applies - Calculator Controller, tab Recipes
scc.gui.reciperules.badge.tip: Applies to every order on this network. See and edit all rules in the Calculator Controller, tab Recipes.
scc.gui.reciperules.badge.title: Network recipe rule
scc.gui.reciperules.card.keys: Shift-click: try %s first · Right-click: never use this recipe
scc.gui.reciperules.card.never.tip: The network never uses %s for this item. Right-click to allow it again.
scc.gui.reciperules.card.never.one.tip: The network never uses this recipe for this item. Right-click to allow it again.
scc.gui.reciperules.delete.tip: The network plans this item as usual again.
scc.gui.reciperules.down.tip: Try this one later. From the last place it leaves the order.
scc.gui.reciperules.empty: No recipe rules yet - the network plans as usual.
scc.gui.reciperules.empty.tip: Rules apply to every order on this network: all players, Requesters, order lists and AE2. In the order window: click a recipe or machine to choose it, Shift-click a recipe card to try its recipe type first, right-click to never use that recipe, Ctrl+right-click to never use its whole type. Or add a rule with the button on the left.
scc.gui.reciperules.never.machine.tip: This machine never gets this recipe type - another one does it, or the plan takes another way.
scc.gui.reciperules.never.toggle.tip: Never build this item with this recipe type - for every order on this network.
scc.gui.reciperules.noentries: The recipe book knows no recipe types here yet - open the order window once after the analysis.
scc.gui.reciperules.pick.machine.tip: Set in the order window by clicking the machine on a recipe card. Only this machine gets the steps while it is on the network.
scc.gui.reciperules.pick.recipe.tip: Set in the order window by clicking a recipe card. Used whenever it can run; otherwise the order below applies.
scc.gui.reciperules.state.auto.tip: No rule - the calculator decides by cost and stock.
scc.gui.reciperules.state.never.tip: Never used - plans and orders skip it.
scc.gui.reciperules.state.rank.tip: Place %s - tried before everything below it, even if another way looks cheaper.
scc.gui.reciperules.tab.materials.tip: Which kind is taken first when a recipe accepts several (any planks, any logs ...).
scc.gui.reciperules.tab.recipes.tip: Which recipe and which machine the network uses for an item.
scc.gui.reciperules.up.tip: Try this one sooner. Without a place yet, it joins the order at the end.
scc.gui.recon.beam.blocked: Beam: no room - the block in front of it must be air
scc.gui.recon.state.blocked: The beam has no room for items: the block in front of the reconstructor must be air.
scc.gui.recon.state.none: Face an Atomic Reconstructor (not its beam side) or a block of air in its beam.
scc.gui.recon.state.nopower: Not enough power: the reconstructor needs at least 1,000 CF per shot.
scc.gui.recon.state.otherlens: This lens runs no recipes - use no lens, the plain Lens or the Lens of Color.
scc.gui.recon.state.pulse: Ready (pulse mode) - the calculator fires the reconstructor only while an item is in the beam.
scc.gui.recon.state.ready: Ready - the reconstructor fires every 5 seconds.
scc.gui.recon.state.redstone: Stopped: the reconstructor has a redstone signal.
scc.gui.redstone.title: Redstone
scc.gui.report.copy.tip: Copy the whole report to the clipboard.
scc.gui.report.job.title: Job report
scc.gui.report.missing.head: Missing from storage
scc.gui.report.missing.title: Order rejected
scc.gui.report.network.title: Network report
scc.gui.report.plan.tip: Open the order again with its crafting plan - change ingredients and recipes there.
scc.gui.report.profile.head: Where the server time goes
scc.gui.report.profile.title: SCC performance
scc.gui.report.settings.head: Server settings - change with /scc <name> <value>
scc.gui.report.settings.title: SCC settings
scc.gui.requester.amount.substance: Counted in mB like the tank - type buckets (16, 2.5k) or mB (500mB); steps are whole buckets
scc.gui.requester.amount.tip: Target amount - click to type (12.5k, 2m, 3*64), buttons or scroll: ±1, Shift ±16, Ctrl ±64
scc.gui.requester.batch.tip: Order size: every order is rounded up to a multiple of this. Click to type a number, right-click or scroll for the usual values, empty or "-" orders exactly what is missing.
scc.gui.requester.click: Right click clears the row, the button on the left pauses it
scc.gui.requester.fluidmode: Counts fluid in the tank (in buckets)
scc.gui.requester.interval.tip: How often this row is checked
scc.gui.requester.quiet.off: Loud: orders of this Requester show popups, play the done sound and appear in the job bar of the terminal. Click: mute.
scc.gui.requester.quiet.on: Muted: orders of this Requester show no popup, play no sound and stay out of the job bar at the top of the terminal (they are still in the job list). Click: loud.
scc.gui.requester.retry.gap: Orders as soon as this is in the network - otherwise tries again in %s
scc.gui.requester.row.toggle.tip: Turns only this row on or off. Item, target, interval and batch stay as they are.
scc.gui.requester.state.jobfailed: last order failed - waits before ordering again
scc.gui.requester.state.low: below target - orders on the next tick
scc.gui.requester.state.noplanner: no player online to plan with
scc.gui.requester.title: Requester
scc.gui.restock.energy.tip: Charges anything that takes FE, straight from the network - in your inventory and in your Curios slots, four times a second, so a drained tool fills while you walk.
scc.gui.restock.feed.list.tip: Whitelist: only food in the food row is eaten. Blacklist: any harmless food except it. An empty row allows any harmless food.
scc.gui.restock.feed.mode.tip: When food from the network is eaten. Never waste: only what fits fully into the hunger bar. When hurt: eat right away as soon as health is missing, even if some is wasted - a full bar heals fastest. Waste at most: also eats food that is a bit bigger than what is missing. Below 3 shanks it always eats.
scc.gui.restock.feed.mode.waste_1: Waste at most half a shank
scc.gui.restock.feed.tip: Eats from the network when you are hungry: highest saturation first, nothing wasted. Harmful food (Rotten Flesh, Spider Eye, Pufferfish, Chorus Fruit, Suspicious Stew) is never eaten unless the food row allows it. Same limits as the other switches.
scc.gui.restock.fluids.tip: Tops up tanks you carry from the network, also in Curios slots: fluids and Mekanism chemicals (hydrogen for the Jetpack, paste for the Canteen). A tank with something in it gets more of the same; an empty one only if it takes exactly one kind - an all-purpose tank stays empty, buckets are never filled.
scc.gui.restock.hint: Place an item or click a slot
scc.gui.restock.magnet.list.tip: Whitelist: only items in the magnet row go into the network. Blacklist: everything except them. An empty row takes everything.
scc.gui.restock.magnet.tip: Items you pick up go straight into the network - not what you drop yourself. Same limits as the other switches: only within antenna range and while the network is running. The magnet row filters what it takes.
scc.gui.restock.quests.tip: Off by default. FTB Quests only counts what is in your inventory. With this on, the terminal also reports what your network holds, so a quest asking for 10,000 iron can tick off from the drives instead of your pockets. Be aware of what that changes: quests complete without you ever holding the item, and progress once counted never drops again. It only reports - nothing is taken or reserved - and it needs the antenna in range like everything else. The whole quest list is checked about every six seconds.
scc.gui.restock.repair.tip: Repairs gear with Mending in your inventory, armor and Curios slots with liquid experience from the network (any fluid tagged c:experience, 20 mB = 1 XP) - like picking up XP orbs, 2 durability per point. Only while the network holds some.
scc.gui.restock.title: Keep in inventory
scc.gui.rules.add.tip: Add a standing order: the network processes incoming items or overflow with your autocrafting.
scc.gui.rules.delete.tip: Removes the rule. Running jobs still finish.
scc.gui.rules.empty.tip: A rule turns what flows into the network into something else, using your autocrafting: "Cobblestone → Stone when it arrives" or "above 10,000 Cobblestone → Gravel". Add one with + in the bar on the left.
scc.gui.rules.input.tip: What the rule processes. Type an item id, a tag such as c:raw_materials or a pattern with *, or click the slot to pick an item. Right-click clears.
scc.gui.rules.maxjobs.tip: How many jobs of this rule may run or wait at the same time (1-8).
scc.gui.rules.mode.inflow.tip: Processes only what newly comes into the network. What was there before stays.
scc.gui.rules.mode.overflow.tip: Keeps this many of each matching item and processes everything above.
scc.gui.rules.output.tip: What to make out of it. Click to pick an item, right-click clears. The network finds the way itself with your machines - the plan has to use the input.
scc.gui.rules.priority: Rule jobs come after your own orders: they never take ingredients a player's job needs, and at most 4 run at once.
scc.gui.rules.smelt.tip: Whatever a furnace makes from each item - handy for tags like c:raw_materials, where every item gives something different.
scc.gui.rules.status.loop: The result matches the input - the rule would loop
scc.gui.rules.status.nocraft: The network cannot make the result - check the machines (retry in 20 s)
scc.gui.rules.status.noinput: The plan found does not use the input (retry in 20 s)
scc.gui.rules.status.nooutput: No furnace result for this item
scc.gui.rules.status.noplanner: No planner: needs a terminal in the network and a player online
scc.gui.rules.status.rejected: Plan rejected - ingredients missing or queue full
scc.gui.rules.toggle.tip: A rule that is off orders nothing. Jobs it already started keep running.
scc.gui.security.add.tip:
Add this player with all four rights.
Take rights away afterwards by clicking the boxes.
scc.gui.security.addteam.none: Empty name field: your own team - but neither you nor the owner is in one.
scc.gui.security.addteam.tip: Add an FTB team: every member gets the ticked rights. Joining or leaving the team takes effect at once.
scc.gui.security.claim.tip: This network has no owner, so right now everyone may do everything on it. That happens when the controller was placed by a machine rather than by hand. Claiming makes it yours.
scc.gui.security.empty: Nobody except the owner has rights here. Type a name below to add somebody.
scc.gui.security.empty.teams: Nobody except the owner has rights here. Type a name and press Player - or press Team to let your whole FTB team in.
scc.gui.security.off: Rights are switched off on this server - nothing in this list has any effect yet.
scc.gui.security.on: Rights are enforced on this server.
scc.gui.security.refresh.tip: Ask the server for the list again.
scc.gui.security.right.build: Build: may open and change the blocks of this network.
scc.gui.security.right.order: Order: may start crafting jobs on this network.
scc.gui.security.right.put: Put: may put items and fluids into the network's storage.
scc.gui.security.right.take: Take: may take items and fluids out of the network's storage.
scc.gui.security.team.gone: The FTB team %s no longer exists - this line has no effect. Remove it with the cross.
scc.gui.security.title: Security Terminal
scc.gui.sides.auto.tip: Ask the machine which face does what: faces that take ingredients become inputs, faces that only give become outputs, fuel slots become fuel. You can still change every face by hand afterwards.
scc.gui.sides.autodrain.tip: Move fluids and Mekanism chemicals that stay in the machine into the network: everything in its output tanks (also when full, from every side the machine gives it out), and once the work is done, what SCC filled in itself and is left over. Never touches the liquid fuel, what a running step needs, or input tanks filled by you or a pipe. Needs a Fluid or Chemical Storage with free space.
scc.gui.sides.autopull.tip: Pull finished results into the network on its own
scc.gui.sides.batch.tip:
How many runs are loaded at once (1-4096) - every ingredient is multiplied with it, and the lock only engages after the last one. Each slot only gets what the machine accepts; a full machine ends the set early.
Click: type a number. Shift-click: double. Right-click: halve. Scroll: +1/-1, Shift +8/-8, Ctrl +64/-64.
scc.gui.sides.dilation.tip: Click: Off, 2x, 4x, 8x. Right-click: one step back. The machine in front runs that much faster while a job uses it, and that costs Chronon from the network every second - 1 for 2x, 4 for 4x, 16 for 8x. Without Chronon it runs at normal speed. Chronon comes from a black hole in the Stellar Cradle.
scc.gui.sides.dilation.title: Time Dilation
scc.gui.sides.fuel.amount.tip: How many should be kept inside the machine
scc.gui.sides.fuel.fe.tip: Keep the machine's energy buffer topped up from the network - for everything that does not run on coal. How much goes through per tick is set by this calculator's tier; on Neutron Star it is more than any machine can take, so no cable is needed at all. Works alongside a fuel item, not instead of it.
scc.gui.sides.fuel.fe.title: Supply energy (FE)
scc.gui.sides.fuel.fluid.hint: A filled bucket (or a fluid dragged in from JEI/EMI) keeps that fluid in the machine's tank instead - if the machine has a tank for it.
scc.gui.sides.fuel.fluid.tip: Keeps %s in the machine's tank, refilled from the network: %s mB. In the tank now: %s mB. Shift+click clears it.
scc.gui.sides.fuel.tip: Click to choose an item that is topped up automatically (blaze powder, coal ...) - shift+click clears it
scc.gui.sides.lock.click: Click: next mode. On a Singularity, Result and Empty also switch Never Empty off.
scc.gui.sides.lock.mode.empty: Empty: the next batch only once nothing of the last one is left in the inventory in front (e.g. the barrel).
scc.gui.sides.lock.mode.off: Off: puts the next batch in as soon as the machine takes it.
scc.gui.sides.lock.mode.redstone: Signal: puts nothing in while a redstone signal reaches this calculator.
scc.gui.sides.lock.mode.result: Result: one batch at a time - the next one only after the result of the last is back in the network.
scc.gui.sides.lock.state.empty: Empty - waits until the machine is empty
scc.gui.sides.lock.state.off: Off - always loads the next batch
scc.gui.sides.lock.state.redstone: Signal - held back while a redstone signal is on
scc.gui.sides.lock.state.result: Result - waits until the result is back
scc.gui.sides.lock.tip: When this calculator may put the next batch in. Off: always. Result: one batch at a time, until its result is back. Empty: not until nothing of the last batch is left in the machine - the brewing stand case. Redstone: held back while a signal is on it. On a Singularity, Result and Empty also switch Never Empty off.
scc.gui.sides.machine.recipes: Click: show what this machine makes in %s
scc.gui.sides.priority.tip: Priority when several machines can run the same recipe: highest goes first, equal priority means the faster one. Left-click raises, right-click lowers, hold Shift for steps of 10. Lower priorities only help while no higher one is working on the order.
scc.gui.sides.res.all.tip: Turns every side of this kind one step further.
scc.gui.sides.res.none.tip: Turns every side of this kind off - nothing of this kind moves until you set a side.
scc.gui.sides.res.reset.tip: Back to automatic for this kind - the behaviour from before 1.3.1.
scc.gui.sides.res.tip.1: Click: next mode (off, input, output, both, fuel), right-click: back. Input: fluid ingredients go in here. Output: fluid results are taken out here. Fuel: liquid fuel goes in here. While every side is on Automatic, fluids go through the item input sides as before - and on a Mekanism machine SCC looks for the side that takes the fluid.
scc.gui.sides.res.tip.2: Click: next mode (off, input, output, both), right-click: back. Input: chemicals from the network go in here. Output: chemical results are taken out here. While every side is on Automatic, SCC tries its own side first and then the others.
scc.gui.sides.reverse.tip: Inserts the ingredients last to first. For altars that want the center item last, e.g. the Enchanting Apparatus of Ars Nouveau. Applies to every recipe of this calculator.
scc.gui.sides.tab.tip: Which kind the side cross shows. Items, fluids and chemicals each have their own sides - like Mekanism's side configuration.
scc.gui.sides.throw.tip: Drop the ingredients onto the block in front instead of putting them into an inventory - for the Petal Apothecary, mana pools, altars and everything else you feed by throwing. Put an Item Collector nearby to bring the result back.
scc.gui.sides.timeout.tip: How long an order may wait for this machine before it gives up on its own. Default: the network setting at the Calculator Controller, else each player's choice in F7. For a slow machine of another mod pick a longer time or Never. Right-click: back.
scc.gui.sides.tip: Click: next mode (off, input, output, both, fuel), right-click: back.
scc.gui.sides.title: Side configuration
scc.gui.sides.trade.tip: Which trade the network uses at this villager. A villager often turns several things into emeralds - paper, wheat, carrots - and without a choice the network simply takes the first one that fits. Pin the one you actually farm. Automatic means: whatever matches.
scc.gui.socket.state.0: No rods - without Energizing Rods nothing is charged.
scc.gui.socket.state.2: Ready - waiting for a recipe in the orb.
scc.gui.socket.state.3: No power - connect an SCC cable or another mod's cable.
scc.gui.socket.state.4: Rods warming up (1 second, like Powah's rods).
scc.gui.socket.title: Energizing Socket
scc.gui.station.anvil.extra.tip: The anvil's right slot. A repair material (Diamond for diamond gear) repairs damaged pieces, an enchanted book goes on the first piece it improves, and the same item as on the left combines the two most damaged pieces into one. Right-click the slot to clear it.
scc.gui.station.anvil.item.tip: The anvil's left slot: which item to repair or to put a book on. Every piece of this kind in storage counts. Right-click the slot to clear it.
scc.gui.station.anvil.levels.tip: The most levels one use of the anvil may cost. Vanilla refuses 40 or more (Too Expensive!), so 39 is the top. Shift: steps of 8.
scc.gui.station.enchant.item.tip: What the enchanting table enchants: a Book or any enchantable item. Click with the item on the cursor, pick it from the list or drag it in from JEI. Right-click the slot to clear it.
scc.gui.station.enchant.keep.tip: How many enchanted ones to keep in storage. Below that, the station takes a plain one from storage and enchants it. Books are ordered when they run out. 0 = off. Shift: steps of 8, Ctrl: 64.
scc.gui.station.enchant.slot.tip: Which of the table's three options to take. Best = the strongest one the network can pay for with its liquid experience and lapis.
scc.gui.storagemon.title: Storage Monitor
scc.gui.storagewarn.hint: Warns from %s%% on. Turn the notice off under F7 - Storage warnings.
scc.gui.storagewarn.title: Storage levels
scc.gui.subtitle: Amount: %s
scc.gui.summary: %s base items, %s items total, %s crafting steps
scc.gui.survey.hint: Put the tool into the quarry's survey slot to apply it.
scc.gui.survey.map.tip: North is up. Frame: the quarry's reach. Green: the area. Gold: the core - the arrow points to where the pit goes.
scc.gui.survey.reset.tip: Back to the area the quarry has now (or to points A and B if it is not loaded).
scc.gui.survey.step: Drag the slider, turn the mouse wheel (Shift ±16, Ctrl ±64) or click the number to type.
scc.gui.terminal.available.tip: Only show craftable items whose ingredients are actually available
scc.gui.terminal.bar.hidden.tip: Items hidden with Shift + middle-click - show them again here (the same list as in F7)
scc.gui.terminal.bar.hole.tip: Use the black hole of a Stellar Cradle in this network as a trash can. Hover over an item and press %s (rebindable under Controls), or click here with an item from your inventory on the cursor. You always confirm first.
scc.gui.terminal.bar.more.tip: Everything that is not on the bar. Right-click an entry to pin it to the bar.
scc.gui.terminal.bar.picktools: Middle click: keep tools in hand
scc.gui.terminal.bar.radio.tip: Keep in inventory, magnet, controller and the middle-click switches of the wireless terminal
scc.gui.terminal.bar.recentrow.tip: Shows your last orders as a row above the pinned items. Off gives the row back to storage.
scc.gui.terminal.bar.scale.tip: Steps through the GUI scale this terminal uses while it is open - the same as Ctrl + dragging the corner grip
scc.gui.terminal.bar.settings.tip: Opens the SCC settings (F7) - designs, sounds, notifications and more
scc.gui.terminal.bar.storeinv.tip: Puts everything from your main inventory into the network. Hotbar, armor, off-hand and wireless terminals stay with you.
scc.gui.terminal.bar.unpinhint: Right-click: move back into the menu
scc.gui.terminal.category.tip: Categories - show only ores, materials, food ...
scc.gui.terminal.chemical.tip: Mekanism chemical - not an item: Transfer Calculators move it, crafting jobs feed it into machines
scc.gui.terminal.controller.tip: Opens the Calculator Controller of the linked network from afar: power, blocks, map and rules - view only. Esc brings you back to this terminal. Works with the terminal in a Curios slot too.
scc.gui.terminal.craftable.tip: Also show items the network can build (highlighted blue)
scc.gui.terminal.empty.category: Nothing under %s. Pick another category on the left.
scc.gui.terminal.empty.storage: Nothing stored yet - face a Storage Connector at a chest or place a storage block.
scc.gui.terminal.explain.tip: Prints what the job is waiting for into the chat
scc.gui.terminal.filter.chemicals.tip: Only Mekanism chemicals (gases, infusions, pigments, slurries)
scc.gui.terminal.filter.craftable.tip: Only entries the network can craft (nothing from storage)
scc.gui.terminal.filter.stored.tip: Only what is in storage - no craftable entries
scc.gui.terminal.filter.tip: Show only craftable or stored entries, fluids, chemicals or a single mod. The choice is remembered.
scc.gui.terminal.filter.title: Filters
scc.gui.terminal.fluid.order: Middle click orders it - made by the Just Transformation Calculator, straight into the tanks
scc.gui.terminal.fluid.tank: With a tank on the cursor: left click fills it, right click adds one bucket (1000 mB). Right click on the grid with a full container pours it in and keeps the container on the cursor - Shift: only one bucket, Ctrl: the empty container goes into storage
scc.gui.terminal.fluid.tip: Left click fills a bucket from storage - shift puts it in your inventory
scc.gui.terminal.hide.tip: Shift + middle click hides this item (F7 > Hidden items shows them again)

scc.guide.autocraft.chatorder: Ordering by chat: /scc order <item> [amount] - for example /scc order minecraft:iron_ingot 64. Needs a linked Wireless Terminal in your inventory or Curios slot, in range of its antenna, and the right "order". It plans like the order window: if ingredients are missing, the chat lists them; otherwise the order starts and the chat shows the estimated time. Tab completes item IDs, items of your network first.
scc.guide.autocraft.crafter: Crafts workbench recipes out of the network on its own. It pulls the ingredients, builds the recipe, and puts the result and any leftovers back. Leftovers are why buckets, moulds and presses do not disappear - the game tells us what survives a recipe, and that goes straight back into storage.
scc.guide.autocraft.eta: Remaining time: while an order runs, the order strip next to the terminal (hover a field), the bar above it and the order window show an estimate such as "~2:30 left". It is measured from the order's own progress, so it needs a few seconds for the first value ("estimating time…") and settles as the order goes on. While the order waits - ingredients missing, no machine, no power, a Blood Altar out of LP - the reason stands there instead of a time. The wireless terminal shows the same.
scc.guide.autocraft.how1: When you order something, the mod plans first: it walks the recipe catalogue down until it reaches things that are in storage, and builds a list of steps out of that. Only then does it hand the plan to the network.
scc.guide.autocraft.how2: Each step goes to a free calculator of the right kind. A Calculation Crafter takes workbench recipes; a Processing Calculator takes whatever machine it stands on. Steps that depend on each other run in order, steps that do not run at the same time.
scc.guide.autocraft.jobs1: The job overview in the terminal says what a job is waiting for: a missing ingredient, a machine with no free slot, a container that is full. A job that cannot get anywhere for long enough fails on its own instead of blocking the queue forever. How long is up to you: for the whole network at the Calculator Controller (clock button: 30 s to 30 min, or Never - then orders wait until a player cancels them), for your own orders in F7 - Waiting orders give up after. A slow machine can get its own time on its Processing Calculator (clock button); that wins over the network, the network over F7.
scc.guide.autocraft.jobs2: A container that destroys items - some storage mods have those - is named in the monitor. That is almost always the answer when items go into a machine and never come back.
scc.guide.autocraft.jobui: Click a job in the list to see every step: which machine or Calculation Crafter does it (click the location to highlight it in the world), how far it is, what is missing and what is reserved from storage. The pause button stops a job without losing anything - machines finish what they already have, and it survives a restart. The Crafting Monitor opens the same window on right-click.
scc.guide.automation.accel: Every Job Accelerator on the network makes autocrafting 25% faster, up to 8 of them (+200%). Calculation Crafters work through their recipes faster - even a Neutron Star crafter, which then crafts more per tick once it is down to one operation per tick. Processing Calculators insert and collect without waiting for their cycle; the machine itself keeps its own speed. Each accelerator draws 5 FE/t and glows while a job runs. How many parallel recipes a crafter runs now depends on its tier alone.
scc.guide.automation.constructor: Places blocks from the network into the world - the counterpart to the Breaking Calculator. It looks in one direction and puts down what is in its list: as a block where there is room, or as a dropped item for machines that want it on the ground.
scc.guide.automation.constructor2: The list can be worked through in order, round robin or at random - the last one is for plantings that should not grow in stripes. Redstone stops it.
scc.guide.automation.craftmon: A panel listing every job the network is running, with its step and what it is waiting for. Right-click for the full report.
scc.guide.automation.craftmon2: Several Crafting or Calculator Monitors share the running jobs: in reading order (top to bottom, left to right) each one shows a different job, the oldest first; the last Crafting Monitor lists whatever is left. Sneak + right-click with an empty hand pins a monitor to job 1 to 9; keep clicking until it says Auto to share again.
scc.guide.automation.craftmon3: Monitors of the same kind side by side on one wall, facing the same way, join into one big screen (up to 8×8). A big Crafting Monitor lists many jobs with progress bars, a big Calculator Monitor shows its job large. Clicks on any block act on the whole screen; breaking or adding a block reshapes it.
scc.guide.automation.destructor: Breaks the block in front of it and puts the drops straight into storage - the counterpart to the Constructor. It only breaks when everything that drops fits into the network; otherwise it waits, so nothing is lost.
scc.guide.automation.destructor2: It breaks like a player holding the tool in its slot: Silk Touch and Fortune work and the tool wears down, stopping at the last point of durability (Mending repairs it from liquid experience in the network). Without a tool it uses its bare hand, so stone and ores stay put. Its list says what may be broken - empty means everything, a blacklist turns it around, and tags like c:ores work too.
scc.guide.automation.destructor3: It skips air, fluids, bedrock, blocks that still hold items and blocks of its own network. Claim mods see a player called [SCC] breaking - if a claim forbids it, the Destructor waits. Redstone stops it. When placed, its front (the side with the glowing symbol) faces you: to break the block below, place it from above or press Turn in its window until it says "Front faces: Down". A wrench turns it too.
scc.guide.automation.emitter: Turns a stock count into a redstone signal. At least: signal once the stock reaches the limit - a farm that switches itself off at 10,000 wheat. At most: signal once it drops to the limit - a furnace that starts when coal falls below 64.
scc.guide.automation.logic: The Logic Calculator is a node editor for the whole network. Drag nodes from the palette onto the board and connect outputs to inputs: sources read what SCC already knows (stock, items on order, power, redstone, time, jobs, machines, players), logic nodes compare and combine numbers, actions order items, emit redstone, send messages, pause calculators or remove surplus. The plan runs on the server twice a second - every tick if it contains a Blinker - with no chests and no extra cables.
scc.guide.automation.logic2: Recipe routes are the special part: connect a Recipe Route node to an Order node, and every order of that node uses exactly the recipes in the route - a known recipe you pick, or your own machine recipe such as "3 Raw Iron in the Enrichment Chamber give 4 Iron Dust". The network default stays the same for every other order.
scc.guide.automation.logic3: Planning orders needs a player online, like the Requester. Plans hold up to 96 nodes and are checked again on the server; editing needs the Build right on secured networks (Remove surplus also the Take right).
scc.guide.automation.logic_ex_iron_alarm: Below 1000 Iron Ingots, the plan orders iron along YOUR recipe route (with Mekanism: Enrichment Chamber 3 Raw Iron -> 4 Iron Dust, then the furnace; otherwise the Blast Furnace). While it produces, a Blinker flashes the redstone output - put a lamp next to the block.
scc.guide.automation.logic_ex_keep_stock: Below the target (1000 Iron Ingots), the network orders what is missing - with the normal recipe of your network. The display shows the stock live. Pick your own item in the Stock and Order nodes.
scc.guide.automation.logic_ex_night_shif: Only at night the plan keeps 4096 Stone Bricks in stock, in batches of 512 - your machines work while you sleep and stay free for you during the day. Change the item for your own building project.
scc.guide.automation.logic_ex_overflow: Above 10,000 Cobblestone, a message appears above your hotbar (at most every 5 minutes) and the redstone output switches on - e.g. a warning lamp or a Toggle Bus that stops the quarry.
scc.guide.automation.logic_ex_power_save: Below 20 % power the redstone output switches on and stays on until power is back above 50 % (the Latch remembers it). Put a Toggle Bus next to the block to cut off less important parts of your network.
scc.guide.automation.logic_ex_storage_di: The stock becomes a redstone strength: every 1000 Cobblestone add one level, up to 15 at 15,000. Lay redstone dust with lamps from the block - the further the light reaches, the fuller your storage. At 15,000 a short message tells you it is full.
scc.guide.automation.logic_nodes: Handy nodes: Blinker (flashes a lamp at an adjustable rate in ticks), Machine (is a calculator's machine idle or full), Job finished (fires when an order completes or fails), Radio send/receive (values between your Logic Calculators, also across networks and dimensions - only your own or your team's channels), Calculator on/off (pauses one Processing Calculator), Player (online or nearby), Remove surplus (moves everything above an amount into a chest next to the block; destroying only with an explicit setting) and Note (text that explains your plan).
scc.guide.automation.logic_share: Sharing: Export copies a short share code (SCC-LOGIC:...) of the selection or the whole plan, Import inserts one next to your plan and tells you if items from missing mods are inside. The Library saves plans with a name as readable text files in config/scc/logic_plans - load, insert or delete them in any world, or swap files with friends.
scc.guide.automation.logic_start1: Open the editor and click "Start with a template" - each template shows a preview and says what it does.
scc.guide.automation.logic_start2: Click a node: the inspector on the right edits it. Hover any field, palette entry or dot for an explanation.
scc.guide.automation.logic_start3: Round dots carry numbers, square dots carry on/off (0 = off). Connections light up while their value is not 0.
scc.guide.automation.logic_start4: Tab hides the side panels for more room; F1 shows all controls.
scc.guide.automation.monitor: Load per calculator over the last minute, plus the warnings that actually matter: a machine with no free slot, a container destroying items, a chemical with no item source. On its face it shows the newest running order - what, how much is done, how many runs are left, and which step it is on - so you can see how far your order is without opening anything.
scc.guide.automation.requester: Keeps up to six items at a target stock level. Falls below it, and it orders what is missing on its own. Each row then rests for its interval, so a new order does not go out every tick while the old one is still running. The last button in a row sets the order size: leave it on "-" and it orders exactly the gap, or pick a number and every order is rounded up to a multiple of it - three missing iron plates become one order of 64, so the furnace runs once instead of twenty times. Left-click steps the number up, right-click down. It can overshoot the target on purpose; that is what ordering in batches means.
scc.guide.automation.requester2: Planning needs a player online, because the recipe catalogue lives on the client. With nobody around, the requester simply waits. The speaker button at the top right mutes a Requester: its orders show no popups, play no sound and stay out of the job bar of the terminal. New rows start switched off: pick the item, amount and interval first, then press the play button left of the item to start it.
scc.guide.automation.rules1: The Rules tab of the controller: tell the network what to do with what arrives, and it places the jobs itself with your autocrafting.
scc.guide.automation.rules2: It arrives - "Cobblestone → Stone": everything that newly comes in is processed; what was there before stays.
scc.guide.automation.rules3: Stock above - "above 10,000 Cobblestone → Gravel": keeps that many and processes the rest.
scc.guide.automation.rules4: The input can be an item, a tag such as c:raw_materials or a pattern with *; the result an item or Furnace result. Rule jobs always come after your own orders and never take ingredients a player's job needs.
scc.guide.cabling.labels1: Rename a block in an anvil before you place it and it keeps that name - like a chest. The name then shows in the window title, in Jade and in every report, so you can tell twenty identical storage connectors apart two weeks later.
scc.guide.cabling.toggle: A piece of cable that opens on a redstone signal. Everything behind it becomes a separate network while the signal is on - the way to switch an outpost off without taking cable apart. Pairs well with the Redstone Emitter.
scc.guide.cosmos.brush1: The Design Brush paints Stellar Gear: Drill, Blade, Bow and every Exo piece. Only the steel takes the colour - brass and the glow of the tier stay.
scc.guide.cosmos.brush2: Choose a design (right-click the air), take the gear into your off hand and right-click the air with the brush. Sneak + right-click still opens the choice.
scc.guide.cosmos.brush3: The design stays on the gear through every Star Anvil upgrade. Standard removes it. Worn Exo shows the design on your character too.
scc.guide.cosmos.catch1: A working Sky Harvester catches every meteor that would fall within its range. Its beam pulls the meteor down to the lens, and the loot goes straight into the network.
scc.guide.cosmos.catch2: A catch costs 10,000 FE from the harvester's network. Without power the meteor falls as usual.
scc.guide.cosmos.catch3: Loot: the same ores as in a Meteorite plus 1 to 3 star matter of the lens tier (with a Basic lens: Star Shards).
scc.guide.cosmos.catch4: Caught meteors leave no crater - a harvester keeps your area clean.
scc.guide.cosmos.intro: Three things from the sky: meteors that fall at night, the Gravity Lift that carries you up and down, and starlight blocks for building. And the Design Brush now paints Stellar Gear too.
scc.guide.cosmos.lift1: Gravity Lift - place two or more in one column. They link up to 64 blocks apart when the shaft between them is free, and a soft beam of light shows the link.
scc.guide.cosmos.lift2: Stand on a lift and jump: you glide up to the next one. Sneak: down to the one below. In the middle of the beam it works too.
scc.guide.cosmos.lift3: No teleport - you really ride, fast and smooth, and you pass through the lifts on your way. No fall damage in the beam.
scc.guide.cosmos.lift4: Each ride costs 50 FE + 5 FE per block. The lift has its own small FE buffer: charge it with any FE cable or a Stellar Distributor with FE Module - no SCC network needed. Connected to an SCC network, the network pays when the buffer is empty.
scc.guide.cosmos.lift5: Several lifts in a column make stops: jump again to continue to the next floor.
scc.guide.cosmos.light1: Starlight Lamp - 4 from glowstone and one star matter. Pulses slowly in the star colour, light level 15.
scc.guide.cosmos.light2: Starlight Glass - 8 from clear glass and one star matter. See-through and glowing.
scc.guide.cosmos.light3: Starlight Path - 6 from three lamps, or 2 per lamp in the stonecutter. A slab with a glowing inlay.
scc.guide.cosmos.light4: Eight blocks of one kind around a dye change their colour: red = Red Dwarf, yellow = Yellow Star, light blue = Blue Giant, white = Neutron Star, purple = Singularity.
scc.guide.cosmos.meteor1: Now and then a meteor falls at night - you see its fiery trail across the sky and hear it coming. Without a Sky Harvester nearby it strikes the ground 24 to 48 blocks from you.
scc.guide.cosmos.meteor2: It leaves a small crater lined with magma, blackstone and basalt. In the middle lies the Meteorite, glowing and smoking for a minute.
scc.guide.cosmos.meteor3: Mine the Meteorite for ores - iron, copper, gold, redstone, lapis, quartz, amethyst, rarely emerald or diamond - and 1 to 3 Star Shards. About every third meteorite adds a bonus: raw ore or an ore block of any installed mod, Diamond and Emerald Ore included (in a modpack also tin, osmium, uranium ...). Endgame ores such as Ancient Debris never come from the sky. Silk Touch keeps the block.
scc.guide.cosmos.meteor4: Craters only replace natural ground. Never in claimed chunks (FTB Chunks and other claim mods), never next to chests or machines - there the meteor burns up in the sky.
scc.guide.cosmos.meteor5: About one night in eight per player. Meteors avoid claimed chunks (FTB Chunks, Open Parties and Claims) and protected areas. Server settings: /scc meteors on|off, /scc meteorChance <percent>, /scc meteorsAvoidClaims on|off. OPs can call one with /scc meteor.
scc.guide.cosmos.meteor6: The message tells you where it struck - for example 37 blocks to the north-east - so you find the crater in the dark.
scc.guide.cosmos.sensor1: Sky Sensor - gives a redstone signal when something happens in the sky. Right-click to choose what it watches.
scc.guide.cosmos.sensor2: Conjunction, a star above a chosen height or at its highest point, a meteor approaching (within 128 blocks), meteor shower, night, day or new moon - on = 15, off = 0. Invert swaps both.
scc.guide.cosmos.sensor3: Harvest factor: the signal strength follows the yield of a star in the Sky Harvester (factor x 5 - 1.0 gives 5, with a conjunction up to 15).
scc.guide.cosmos.sensor4: A comparator reads a graded value: how high the star stands (0-90° as 0-15), how close a conjunction is to its peak, how many meteors are coming, how full the moon is.
scc.guide.cosmos.sensor5: It needs no network, power or open sky - it reads the same sky calculation as the Sky Harvester and the Star Chart. Only in dimensions with the SCC sky objects.
scc.guide.cosmos.shard: Star Shard - nine make a Red Dwarf Ember.
scc.guide.cosmos.shower1: Every new moon night is a meteor shower night. At sunset a message announces it: "A meteor shower lights up the sky tonight!"
scc.guide.cosmos.shower2: All night long shooting stars streak across the sky - harmless, only to look at.
scc.guide.cosmos.shower3: And instead of at most one, about 4 real meteors fall per player - with all the usual rules (no claims, no bases, no water). A Sky Harvester in range catches them as always.
scc.guide.cosmos.shower4: Server settings: /scc meteorShowers on|off, /scc meteorShowerEvery <n> (every n-th new moon), /scc meteorShowerMeteors <count>. /scc sky shower tells when the next one comes; OPs jump there with /scc sky shower jump. F7 switches the shooting stars off on your screen.
scc.guide.cradle.build: The core in the middle, eight Star Forge Frames around it on the same level - the same frames as the forge - and four Confinement Coils on the corners, one block higher. The two blocks above the core stay free: that is where the star floats.
scc.guide.cradle.build2: Connect it like the forge: a cable to any frame or under the core. Right-click any part of the formed cradle to open it.
scc.guide.cradle.cradle: Ignites a star from a seed and holds it in a magnetic cage. The star lives its whole life above the core and gives power the whole time.
scc.guide.cradle.hole1: It eats items and fluids from the network according to its diet: 20,000 FE per item, 20 FE per mB, at most 40,000 FE/t. That is 2 items per tick - a proper cobblestone farm.
scc.guide.cradle.hole2: It has no lifetime as long as it is fed. Without food it evaporates after 30 minutes. +25 % at new moon.
scc.guide.cradle.hole3: It only takes from the network, and every item counts the same - what is inside a shulker box does not count. The best trash can in the pack, and it gives power back.
scc.guide.cradle.hole4: Chronon: while it eats, the black hole condenses time. Every 40 food items (a bucket counts as one) make one Chronon - about 1 per second at full feeding. It goes straight into the network, or into the output slot if the network is full. Singularity Processing Calculators pay for Time Dilation with it (setting: cradleFoodPerChronon).
scc.guide.cradle.hole5: You can also throw items in by hand: in any terminal of the network, hover over an item and press Delete. This works for items that are not in the diet too - they count like normal food.
scc.guide.cradle.interference: Gravitational interference: all cradles in the same network or within 64 blocks are ranked by output. The strongest gives 100 %, the second 50 %, then 25 %, 12.5 % ... The window shows the value.
scc.guide.cradle.interference2: Two or three cradles are worth it, twenty are not.
scc.guide.cradle.keep: Keep burning (button on the left): pick a seed class and the cradle keeps itself going. When the star is gone it takes a new seed from the network - or orders one through autocrafting - and ignites it. Sun Cores and Neutronium come in the same way, one at a time, exactly when they are used. Before a supernova it warns you if your storage cannot hold the barrier. Dark Matter is never taken: the collapse is your decision.
scc.guide.cradle.l.black_hole: Black Hole: put 4 Dark Matter into a pulsar and it collapses.
scc.guide.cradle.l.blue_giant: Blue Giant: 2,500 FE/t for 3 hours, then a supernova. Each Neutronium in the matter slot makes it 30 minutes older - 6 trigger the supernova right away.
scc.guide.cradle.l.pulsar: Pulsar: 10,000 FE/t on average, in bursts every two seconds - without Energy Storage half of it is lost. It spins down from 150 % to 50 % over 6 hours; each Neutronium spins it up by 20 minutes. +25 % at full moon.
scc.guide.cradle.l.red_dwarf: Red Dwarf: 80 FE/t for 24 hours, then it fades.
scc.guide.cradle.l.supernova: Supernova: for ten seconds the coils charge a barrier of 2,000,000 FE from the network. If it holds: 2 Neutronium and a pulsar. If not: the cradle falls apart and the coils drop as items. No crater.
scc.guide.cradle.l.yellow_star: Yellow Star: 500 FE/t for 10 hours, +25 % by day. Every Sun Core in the matter slot adds 30 minutes.
scc.guide.cradle.life1: Small stars burn long and faint, big ones short and bright.
scc.guide.cradle.life2: Time only runs while the cradle's chunk is loaded: an unloaded star does not age, but gives nothing either. All numbers can be changed on the server with /scc (cradle...).
scc.guide.cradle.merge: Black holes within 64 blocks merge: the older one absorbs the younger one and gets +10,000 FE/t on its limit - so it also eats 10 more items per second. By default a black hole absorbs one other; server settings cradleHoleMerges (how many, 0 = never merge) and cradleHoleMergeBonus (FE/t each).
scc.guide.cradle.power: Power goes into the network like from a Transfer Calculator in FE mode: into the Energy Storages, then into the controller buffer. What the network cannot take waits in the core, and cables of other mods can pull it out.
scc.guide.cradle.redstone: The core gives a redstone signal while the star is about to die - enough for a lamp or a bell.
scc.guide.cradle.seeds.blue: Star Forge: Yellow Star Seed + 4 Blue Plasma.
scc.guide.cradle.seeds.ignite: Ignition costs a charge from the network: 20,000 FE (red), 200,000 FE (yellow), 1,000,000 FE (blue).
scc.guide.cradle.seeds.red: Star Forge: shell + 4 Red Dwarf Ember.
scc.guide.cradle.seeds.shell: Crafting table: glass, gold, amethyst and a block of redstone. The empty shell for every seed.
scc.guide.cradle.seeds.yellow: Star Forge: Red Dwarf Seed + 4 Sun Core.
scc.guide.distributor.charge: Charging Module - charges the gear of every player in range who may take from the network (Security Terminal), inventory and Curios slots, without a wireless terminal. It also tops up their tanks with fluids and Mekanism chemicals (hydrogen for the Jetpack, paste for the Canteen) - like Refill tanks on the Wireless Terminal. Only single items are charged, never stacks. The Refill tanks button turns the tank top-up off.
scc.guide.distributor.cost1: 4 FE/t on its own plus 0.1 FE/t per supplied block - on top of the power it hands out.
scc.guide.distributor.cost2: Transfer loss: nothing up to 16 blocks, then 1% per 16 blocks, at most 10%.
scc.guide.distributor.cost3: Beyond 256 blocks (Infinite Range) 15%, into another dimension 25%.
scc.guide.distributor.cost4: A cable is still the cheapest way to power a machine - the distributor is paid comfort. With Keep reserve it pauses before the network runs low.
scc.guide.distributor.fe: FE Module - pushes FE from the network into every block in range that takes power. Blocks that also give power out (capacitor banks, energy cubes) count as batteries and are left out unless you switch on Include batteries - otherwise power would loop between network and battery. Machines with their own buffer, inventory or tanks (Industrial Foregoing, Just Dire Things, FTB Stuff & Things, Garden Cloche) count as consumers. Pack makers can sort blocks with the block tags scc:distributor_consumer and scc:distributor_battery. Blocks of this mod are never supplied.
scc.guide.distributor.fe2: Machines that only take power on one side work too: the distributor finds that side by itself.
scc.guide.distributor.fe3: Entry points of other energy networks are never supplied, not even with Include batteries: the Flux Plug (Flux Networks), the Flux Accessor (Applied Flux) and the Quantum Entangloporter (Mekanism). The network's power would only drain into the other network or run in a circle. Pack makers can add more blocks to the block tag scc:distributor_ignored. Powah reactors are never supplied either - they are not in the list and cannot be linked (block tag scc:distributor_never).
scc.guide.distributor.linked1: Area (the default) supplies everything in range. Linked supplies only the blocks you pick - this applies to power; Source always goes to the whole area. In Area mode the x at the end of a row excludes a block for good, the + takes it back, and Clear exclusions takes all of them back. A Network Tool linked to the distributor does the same in the world: shift-right-click a block to exclude it or take it back.
scc.guide.distributor.linked2: Take a Network Tool and shift-right-click the distributor: the tool now links to it.
scc.guide.distributor.linked3: Shift-right-click a block to add it, again to remove it. While you hold the tool, beams show what already belongs. The x at the end of a row in the window unlinks a block - also one that is gone.
scc.guide.distributor.linked4: Shift-right-click the air to let the tool go.
scc.guide.distributor.list1: The list in the window names every block with its state: supplied, full, battery, over the tier's limit - in Linked mode also no FE, not loaded or out of range. Hover a row for position and loss. Show links draws beams to the supplied ones.
scc.guide.distributor.list2: It searches every five seconds, in loaded chunks only and shared by all distributors of a dimension, and hands out power twice a second - a busy base stays smooth.
scc.guide.distributor.range1: 16 blocks without an upgrade, as a cube around the block - Show range draws it in the world.
scc.guide.distributor.range2: Range Upgrades: 32 blocks each, up to 8 (256 blocks).
scc.guide.distributor.range3: Infinite Range Upgrade: the whole dimension. Dimensional Upgrade: every dimension. Only loaded chunks count, and the distributor never loads one.
scc.guide.distributor.slotclick: Click an empty slot in the window: the part comes straight from your SCC network - or the order window opens if it is not in storage (Ctrl+click orders right away). Works in every SCC window with upgrade, module or card slots: Star Quarry, Sky Harvester, Network Antenna and more.
scc.guide.distributor.source: Source Module - every Ars Nouveau block in range draws the network's Source, however short its own reach is. This is the way to hand out the network's Source; the Interface no longer does it.
scc.guide.distributor.tiers2: Throughput counts power and charging together. All numbers are server settings - /scc list shows them (distRate..., distTargets..., distLoss...).
scc.guide.distributor.what: A network block that reaches everything around it without cables. Put modules into it: power for machines, Source for Ars blocks, charge for players. It comes in all six tiers and goes up in the Star Forge like every other device.
scc.guide.distributor.what2: Right-click it for the window: range and module slots at the top, below that a line saying what it does right now and a list of every block it supplies or leaves out - with the reason.
scc.guide.energy.cradle: Ignites a star seed from the Star Forge and turns the star's whole life into power - day and night, far more than photons.
scc.guide.energy.dist: With an FE Module it powers every machine around it - machines of other mods too - straight from the network. Handy for a crowded workshop; a cable is still the cheaper way.
scc.guide.energy.harvester: In photon mode it collects starlight and feeds it into the network. It needs no power itself, so it can start an empty network.
scc.guide.energy.s1: Step 1: a generator from another mod
scc.guide.energy.s1a: Your pack has generators? Run their power cable into the Calculator Controller, or put a Transfer Calculator in FE mode on the generator. That is all it takes - the steps below are your own sources for later, or for a pack without any.
scc.guide.energy.s2a: Build it: the harvester, two Harvester Masts on top, a cable underneath, open sky above the lens.
scc.guide.energy.s2b: Put in a Basic Lens - four glass, four amethyst shards and a gold ingot. Every better lens is forged from it.
scc.guide.energy.s2c: Click the Matter/Photons switch on the left of its window. The Basic Lens gives 50 to 70 FE/t, enough for a small network; the best lenses give up to 1,600 FE/t each.
scc.guide.energy.s2d: Rain stops it, and photon harvesters within 16 blocks share the sky - spread them out. The Star Chart shows a photon forecast for the next Minecraft day.
scc.guide.energy.s3: Step 3: a star of your own
scc.guide.energy.s3a: Real time, while the chunk is loaded. A Blue Giant ends in a supernova: if the coils can charge a 2,000,000 FE barrier from the network, a Pulsar remains. Feed it 4 Dark Matter and it collapses into a Black Hole that eats your junk and turns it into power.
scc.guide.energy.s5: Step 5: keep an eye on it
scc.guide.energy.s5a: Open the controller and click the Power tab: generation by source against consumption by group, how long your storage lasts, and a chart of the last Minecraft day. Jade shows generation and draw when you look at the controller.
scc.guide.energy.s5b: On a shortage the network does not simply go dark. It switches groups off one by one - Sky Harvesters, distributors and charging first, crafters last - while cables, storage and terminals keep running. Change the order in the same tab, or switch load shedding off there.
scc.guide.energy.storage: The network's battery. Every source below fills it, and it carries you through the night and the rain. Build one early.
scc.guide.energy.why1: Power mode is on: every block of the network costs a little FE per tick - a cable 0.1, a terminal 1, a crafter 2. The controller pays from its own buffer first, then from your Energy Storages. When both are empty, the network stops until power comes back. This chapter is the way from the first FE to a base that powers itself.
scc.guide.energy.why2: Just want to try the mod first? An operator can switch power off with /scc power off - then everything runs for free.
scc.guide.first.antenna: Place a Network Antenna on the network. Wireless terminals log in here - range 32 blocks, more with Range Upgrades.
scc.guide.first.cable: Run cable from the controller to where your chests and machines are.
scc.guide.first.clicks: Click a picture to see its recipe in JEI or EMI. Lines starting with » jump to the chapter with the details.
scc.guide.first.controller: Place it first - one per network. Every other SCC block has to be connected back to it.
scc.guide.first.crafter: Place a Calculation Crafter on the network. From now on every workbench recipe can be ordered whose ingredients are in storage - the whole tree, sticks and planks included.
scc.guide.first.fuel: A furnace needs fuel: fill it by hand, or put a Supply Module into the calculator's window and it keeps the fuel topped up from storage.
scc.guide.first.furnace: Place a Processing Calculator against a furnace, touching the network. It recognises the furnace by itself: from now on, ordering iron ingots smelts raw iron on the way. It works the same with almost any modded machine.
scc.guide.first.intro: New to SCC? Do these steps in order. After about half an hour you have a network that stores everything, crafts on order, runs a furnace for you and keeps stock on its own.
scc.guide.first.next.forge: Raises blocks, upgrade stones and lenses a tier with star matter, and makes the seeds for the Stellar Cradle.
scc.guide.first.next.integrations: Integrations: AE2, Refined Storage, Mekanism, Create, Ars Nouveau, Jade, JEI/EMI and more.
scc.guide.first.next.modules: Modules for the Processing Calculator: Routing for fussy machines and multiblocks, Supply for fuel and power, Custom Pattern for machines JEI does not know.
scc.guide.first.next.sky: A tower with a lens that harvests the sky: star matter for the higher tiers, and photons - SCC's own power source.
scc.guide.first.next.tiers: Upgrade a placed block a tier: faster steps, more parallel jobs, more range - from Basic up to Singularity.
scc.guide.first.next0: Your base runs. Pick what you need next:
scc.guide.first.order: Middle-click an item in the terminal to order it (or click one that is craftable but not in stock). The order window shows what comes from storage, what gets crafted and what is missing - confirm, and the network does the rest. Ctrl+middle-click tells you why something cannot be built.
scc.guide.first.power1: The network runs on FE. Run a generator's power cable into the Calculator Controller, or put a Transfer Calculator in FE mode on the generator. An Energy Storage on the cable keeps the network running through gaps.
scc.guide.first.power2: No generator in your pack yet? The Power Supply chapter shows SCC's own sources. Just want to look around first? An operator can type /scc power off and everything runs for free.
scc.guide.first.requester: A Requester keeps up to six items at a level you set - say 64 torches or 256 iron ingots. When stock drops below, it orders the gap on its own.
scc.guide.first.storage: Put a Storage Connector on a chest or barrel you already have - its contents now belong to the network. No chest? An Item Storage (second recipe) placed on the cable is storage on its own.
scc.guide.first.store1: Open the terminal and shift-click items in your inventory - they go straight into storage. Shift + double-click stores every stack of that item at once. Click an item in the list to take a stack, right-click for half. Type in the search bar to find anything.
scc.guide.first.store2: Nothing shows as craftable? The recipe catalogue is built from JEI or EMI on your client the first time you open a terminal - give it a moment, or pick Re-scan recipes in the terminal menu (three dots).
scc.guide.first.terminal: Place it on the cable and open it: everything in storage in one searchable list.
scc.guide.first.terminal2: Right-click the antenna once with the Wireless Terminal to link it. After that it opens anywhere in range, ordering included.
scc.guide.first.touch: Blocks belong to one network if they touch or are joined by cable. A terminal placed straight onto the controller works too.
scc.guide.forge.build: The core in the middle, eight Star Forge Frames around it on the same level, and one to four Focus Pylons on the corners, one block higher. The space above the core stays free - that is where the reaction happens. Connect a cable to any frame or under the core: the whole forge counts as one network block.
scc.guide.forge.build2: Every pylon charges the forge with up to 250,000 FE per tick from the network. With power off in the world config, forging is free and only takes its two seconds.
scc.guide.forge.events.collapse: Neutron Star to Singularity: the light shrinks, a glowing disc spins up around a black core, and everything falls into a point.
scc.guide.forge.events.supernova: Blue Giant to Neutron Star: the star swells, turns white and explodes - a supernova, with a shockwave rolling over the forge.
scc.guide.forge.forge: Raises a block, an upgrade stone or a lens one tier. Put the item in, add the matter of the new tier - for lenses from Yellow Star up, the lens prism - and the pylons fire.
scc.guide.forge.formed: Once everything stands, the thirteen blocks form into one machine: a platform with arms that unfold, crystal heads that fire the lasers and two rings around the focus. Right-click any part to open it. Take one block away and it falls apart into single blocks again.
scc.guide.forge.network1: Connected to the network, the forge is a machine of its own - no Processing Calculator needed. Order a Singularity Processing Calculator from the terminal and it plans the whole chain: the forge takes in every step, every stone and all the matter, and sends the results to storage. A Processing Calculator already at the core keeps working as before.
scc.guide.forge.network2: Five of the same order go through as one stack.
scc.guide.forge.preview: Hold a frame or a pylon near the core: ghost blocks show where parts are still missing.
scc.guide.forge.use1: One step takes about two seconds - no matter if it is one item or a whole stack: up to 64 go through in a single reaction.
scc.guide.forge.use2: It always goes one tier at a time: Basic to Red Dwarf, Red Dwarf to Yellow Star and so on. Filled storage blocks keep their contents.
scc.guide.forge.use3: A filled storage block can be forged without emptying it first.
scc.guide.integrations.ae2a: With AE2 installed, the Network Antenna also registers as an AE2 wireless access point. That is not for AE2 itself - it is the hook other mods look for when they ask "is there a network here I may build from".
scc.guide.integrations.ae2b: The antenna keeps its own range and its own rules; nothing of an AE2 network is imported, and no AE2 channel is used.
scc.guide.integrations.ae2c: Without AE2 the antenna is an ordinary SCC block - only the mods below then find no access point.
scc.guide.integrations.ae2d: And the other way round: a Storage Connector facing an ME Interface uses the whole ME network as storage - read, insert, extract - instead of the interface's nine slots. Both directions on the same AE2 network are safe; each side sees what really lies on the other.
scc.guide.integrations.ae2e: A Storage Connector works on any block of an AE2 network - controller, cable, drive or ME Interface. Everything on the disks shows up in the SCC terminal, and everything the AE2 network has a pattern for is listed as craftable. Order it and SCC hands the job to AE2 instead of building it itself - AE2 takes the ingredients from its own storage, and the result lands in the network you are looking at.
scc.guide.integrations.ae2f: Has the AE2 network a pattern for it? Then the job goes to AE2, and the entry carries a small AE2 mark in the terminal so you can see who is building what. Everything else SCC builds itself.
scc.guide.integrations.ae2g: Hybrid mode: when the Network Antenna touches an AE2 network (a cable or controller right next to it), it tells AE2 what SCC can build - only the things AE2 has no pattern for. An AE2 job whose ingredient has no AE2 pattern no longer waits forever: AE2 lists the ingredient as craftable, SCC builds it as an ordinary SCC job (same power, same costs, visible in the job list) and hands the result straight to the waiting AE2 job. Such items can also be ordered directly in the AE2 terminal.
scc.guide.integrations.ae2h: SCC plans with the recipe viewer, so a player has to be online. With security on, whoever placed the antenna needs the order right. The list is renewed only when machines or patterns change, at most once a minute. Switch it off with /scc ae2Provider off. The list shows up even on an ME network without a crafting CPU; to order in AE2 you need one.
scc.guide.integrations.ars1: Source Storage, six tiers, crafted from Source Gems around a Source Jar. To Ars every one of them is a Source Jar - relays fill it, machines nearby drink from it - but behind it stands the Source of the whole network. A Storage Connector facing an ordinary Source Jar adds that jar to the pool.
scc.guide.integrations.ars4: Source Module in a Stellar Distributor: Source for every Ars block in its range, with a list of what it reaches. It replaces the old Interface Source Upgrade - an old upgrade turns into a Source Module.
scc.guide.integrations.avaritia1: The Sculk (3x3), Nether (5x5), End (7x7) and Extreme Crafting Table (9x9) of Re:Avaritia have no output slot - the result only exists in the table's window. Put a Processing Calculator in front of one: SCC places every ingredient in the cell the recipe asks for, takes the result out the way a player would and sends it back to the network.
scc.guide.integrations.avaritia2: One set at a time: the next one goes in once the grid is empty. A recipe made for one table only runs on that table, just like by hand - an Extreme recipe needs an Extreme Crafting Table. The tables of Extended Crafting work the same way.
scc.guide.integrations.ctrl1: A controller gathers many chests and presents itself as one huge inventory. Storing goes through it; reading does not - SCC reads the chests behind it directly.
scc.guide.integrations.ctrl2: The reason is a real case: a controller reported 27 slots for chests that had 108. Everything beyond the reported slot was invisible, and things put there looked lost. If SCC finds such a case it says so in the log and reads past the controller from then on.
scc.guide.integrations.curios1: A wireless terminal also counts when it sits in a Curios slot instead of your inventory - for the keybind, for Construction Sticks and for anything else that looks for a terminal on you.
scc.guide.integrations.draconic1: Put a Processing Calculator in front of a Fusion Crafting Core: orders from the network run there - SCC puts the catalyst into the core and each ingredient into its own free injector, starts the fusion like the button in the core's window and collects the result. Recipes shown by JEI/EMI are planned like any other machine recipe, also those with more than 9 ingredients.
scc.guide.integrations.draconic2: Build the injectors as usual and give them power - they charge themselves like always. One set at a time; a recipe needs as many injectors as it has ingredients and injectors of the right tier, just like by hand.
scc.guide.integrations.effortless1: Carry a linked wireless terminal (inventory or Curios slot) and stay within antenna range: Effortless Building then counts the blocks in your network as available and takes what is missing from your inventory straight out of storage - the same way it works with an AE2 wireless terminal.
scc.guide.integrations.effortless2: Order: your inventory first, then AE2 (if present), then the SCC network. Afterwards the stack in your hand is topped up from the network. You need the "take" right on secured networks, items reserved for a running job stay untouched, and broken blocks do not go back into the network. Creative mode is unchanged.
scc.guide.integrations.effortless3: The preview count next to the crosshair is marked "SCC" and refreshes about once a second. Out of range or without a terminal, Effortless Building shows missing blocks as usual.
scc.guide.integrations.eio1: The SCC Network Conduit works exactly like a Network Cable, but shares a bundle with Ender IO's item, fluid and energy conduits. You get 3 from 6 Conduit Binders and 3 Network Cables. The Yeta Wrench disconnects it like any other conduit.
scc.guide.integrations.eio2: Storage Connectors also work with Ender IO tanks and capacitor banks. Without Ender IO the conduit and its recipe do not exist.
scc.guide.integrations.gadgets1: Both build straight out of the network: link the gadget to the antenna (Building Gadgets: put it into the antenna's slot and press Link, or sneak + right-click the antenna with the gadget in Bind mode) or simply carry a linked wireless terminal (Construction Sticks), and the blocks you place come from storage instead of your inventory. Blocks you break or undo go back into the network.
scc.guide.integrations.gadgets2: Building Gadgets asks the AE2 access point, Construction Sticks ask their own container manager - two different paths for the same thing, and SCC answers both.
scc.guide.integrations.gadgets3: The preview of a gadget is drawn on your own machine and does not ask the server - a preview that shows up does not prove the network has the blocks.
scc.guide.integrations.goo1: Goo recipes do not run through JEI categories, so they would be missing from the scan. SCC reads them out of the recipe manager itself - spreading, tag spreading and fluid drops.
scc.guide.integrations.goo2: The transformation calculator runs the fluid conversions - and it runs them itself, without buckets: input fluid out of the tanks, catalyst item out of storage, result back into the tanks. Right-click it and set one row per fluid with how much should be kept ready. It works out the chain on its own, so asking for Time Fluid also makes the Polymorphic Fluid it needs - in one step, without a tank for the stage in between. Give a stage its own row only if you want it in stock as well.
scc.guide.integrations.goo3: A goo block has no inventory at all - it replaces blocks in the world. So these two calculators do the conversion themselves: goo item in the slot decides the tier, ingredients come out of storage, the result goes straight back in.
scc.guide.integrations.jade: Jade - the answer where you are looking
scc.guide.integrations.jade1: Every block of this mod writes its own line into Jade's tooltip: how large the network is and whether it runs, what a calculator is waiting for, how full a storage is, what a monitor watches, why a job is stuck. A network of fifty blocks otherwise means opening fifty windows to find the one that is stuck.
scc.guide.integrations.jei: JEI and EMI - where the recipes come from
scc.guide.integrations.jei1: The recipe viewer is the most important integration of them all. Without JEI or EMI, SCC only knows the recipes Minecraft itself hands out - crafting, smelting, stonecutting, smithing. With one of them, SCC sees every machine recipe of every mod in the pack, because the viewer already had to collect them to show them to you. If both are installed, SCC reads from JEI.
scc.guide.integrations.jei2: The scan reads JEI's categories and the machines that belong to them - that is how the network knows which block a recipe needs.
scc.guide.integrations.jei3: Drag an item or fluid out of JEI or EMI onto a filter slot, a template or a request line and it is set - in every window of this mod that has such slots.
scc.guide.integrations.jei4: The + button on a JEI or EMI recipe fills the crafting terminal from the network, and ingredients the network is missing are marked red in every recipe. Hold Ctrl while clicking + and everything the network is missing is ordered right away - it drops into the grid on its own once it is built.
scc.guide.integrations.jei5: Without a recipe viewer the network still runs, it just knows far fewer ways to build something. The log says which source was used after every scan.
scc.guide.integrations.l.ae2: Applied Energistics 2 - a Storage Connector on any AE2 block uses the whole ME network as storage, AE2 patterns can be ordered from the SCC terminal, and the Network Antenna also answers as an AE2 wireless access point.
scc.guide.integrations.l.ars: Ars Nouveau - Source Storage: the network's Source, seen by every Ars machine as a jar.
scc.guide.integrations.l.avaritia: Avaritia (Re:Avaritia) - a Processing Calculator in front of a Sculk, Nether, End or Extreme Crafting Table lays out the grid and takes the result.
scc.guide.integrations.l.cobblemon: Cobblemon - a Processing Calculator in front of a cooking pot on a campfire cooks its recipes: ingredients in the right pattern, lid closed, dish back into the network. Also the Better Campfire Pot.
scc.guide.integrations.l.curios: Curios - a wireless terminal counts from a Curios slot, not only from your inventory.
scc.guide.integrations.l.effortless: Effortless Building - lines, walls and shapes are built out of the network while you carry a linked wireless terminal.
scc.guide.integrations.l.enderio: Ender IO - the SCC Network Conduit carries your network through conduit bundles, next to item, fluid and energy conduits.
scc.guide.integrations.l.gadgets: Building Gadgets 2 - builds straight out of the network once the gadget is linked to the antenna (Link button, or Bind mode on the antenna).
scc.guide.integrations.l.ifsouls: Industrial Foregoing Souls - Soul Storage: souls as a network resource, Soul Pipes at the SCC Interface.
scc.guide.integrations.l.jade: Jade - a line of its own at every block of this mod: size, state, and what it is waiting for.
scc.guide.integrations.l.jei: JEI / EMI - the source of nearly every recipe SCC knows, plus drag and drop into every filter slot.
scc.guide.integrations.l.justdire: Just Dire Things - goo and transformation recipes, which JEI does not hand out.
scc.guide.integrations.l.lognet: Logistics Networks - a node on an Interface works with the whole network, and the LN Wrench links to a Calculator Controller just as it does to an ME Controller.
scc.guide.integrations.l.mek: Mekanism - chemicals count as a resource of the network, and its conversions are read from JEI.
scc.guide.integrations.l.powah: Powah - the Energizing Socket: the Energizing Orb stands on it, real Energizing Rods go inside.
scc.guide.integrations.l.qed: Excessive Utilities - the QED has no inventory to the outside; SCC gives it one.
scc.guide.integrations.l.quests: FTB Quests - item tasks are filled out of storage instead of out of your pockets.
scc.guide.integrations.l.raven: Apothic Enchanting - a Processing Calculator in front of an Enchanting Table of the Raven runs infusion recipes and sets the table's stats for each one; in front of a normal enchanting table its bookshelves count.
scc.guide.integrations.l.rs: Refined Storage 2 - a Storage Connector on any RS block uses the whole RS network as storage, RS patterns can be ordered from the SCC terminal, and an RS External Storage in front of the Network Antenna sees the SCC network.
scc.guide.integrations.l.sticks: Construction Sticks - the same, through a linked wireless terminal you carry.
scc.guide.integrations.l.storage: Sophisticated Storage and other chest controllers - SCC reads the real chests behind them.
scc.guide.integrations.l.villagers: Easy Villagers - a villager in front of a Processing Calculator becomes a machine.
scc.guide.integrations.list: The mods SCC knows, and what it does with each of them. The big ones have their own section further down on this page. Anything not listed still works through the normal ways: storage blocks, Storage Connectors and Processing Calculators work with nearly every machine that has an inventory.
scc.guide.integrations.ln1: Logistics Networks nodes sit on SCC blocks like on any other container: storage blocks, the Interface, Processing Calculators, and the Calculator Controller for energy.
scc.guide.integrations.ln2: A node on an Interface works with the whole network, just like on an ME Interface - since Logistics Networks 1.17 only with a Network Upgrade in the node (without it, the node sees the nine slots like a chest). A Sender takes what the Interface's templates hand out - items, and fluids dragged from JEI or EMI onto a template - in any amount, not only what lies in its slots. A Receiver puts everything straight into storage, fluids included. Items a running job has reserved stay where they are. Without power or storage, the node uses the nine slots.
scc.guide.integrations.ln3: Shift + right-click a Calculator Controller with the LN Wrench to link it - the wrench then reads "SCC".
