scc.guide.special.wormhole_redstone: A gate gives a redstone signal of 15 for one second whenever someone arrives at it or jumps away from it - for a door to the arrival room, a light or a counter. Jumps with the Wormhole Remote make the target gate pulse too.
scc.guide.special.wormhole_remote: A Wormhole Gate for your pocket. Link it like a Wireless Terminal - right-click a Network Antenna, or right-click a Wormhole Gate directly. Right-click into the air: the same list as at a gate, measured from where you stand. Pick a gate and a rift opens two to three blocks in front of you, for 10 seconds. Walk in and you arrive on top of that gate.
scc.guide.special.wormhole_remote2: Opening the rift costs the gate price for the same trip plus 50% (setting: wormholeRemoteCost), paid from the network above the controller's reserve. Anyone may follow you through while it is open (wormholeRemoteShared). If the target gate disappears or the network goes offline before anyone went through, the rift collapses and the power goes back. After opening, the remote recharges for 30 seconds (wormholeRemoteCooldown; wormholeRemoteOpen sets how long the rift stays).
scc.guide.special.wormhole_remote3: Range works like the Wireless Terminal: linked to an antenna, you need to be within its range - in another dimension only with a Dimensional Upgrade in that antenna. Linked to a gate, the best antenna of the network counts; without any antenna, only 32 blocks around the gate.
scc.guide.special.wormhole_remote4: A rift needs open ground in front of you and cannot be opened through a wall, at spawn or in someone else's claim. With security on, it needs the build right on the network - like jumping from a gate.
scc.guide.special.wormhole_style: Right-click the tunnel itself to open the gate's window - no need to aim at the base (sneak to use items through it). The base takes a Facade like a cable: right-click it with a Facade of any full block, sneak-right-click with the Wrench to take it off - the portal above stays as it is. Pick a portal color at the bottom of the window; a Remote's rift shows the color of its target gate.
scc.guide.start.cable: Bridges distance. Cables connect to each other and to any SCC block they touch.
scc.guide.start.connector: Place it against a chest, barrel or tank. That container is now network storage.
scc.guide.start.controller: The heart of the network. One per network, and everything else has to be connected back to it. When power mode is on, it is also the only place energy goes in.
scc.guide.start.s1b: Place the Calculator Controller. The network runs on power (FE): the next chapter, Power Supply, shows where it comes from - with or without other mods.
scc.guide.start.s2: Run cable from it to a chest and put a Storage Connector on the chest.
scc.guide.start.s3: Put a Network Terminal anywhere on the cable and open it - the contents of the chest are the list.
scc.guide.start.s4: Add a Calculation Crafter for workbench recipes.
scc.guide.start.s5: Put a Processing Calculator on every machine the network should be allowed to use.
scc.guide.start.scan: If the terminal shows your items but nothing is craftable, the recipe catalogue has not been built yet. It is built from JEI or EMI on your own client - see the last chapter.
scc.guide.start.terminal: Your window into the network: everything in storage, searchable, plus the order screen.
scc.guide.start.toolbar1: Every block window has a toolbar on its left edge. Each icon shows its state at a glance - a lit or unlit redstone torch, arrows in or out, a white or black list, a gold rim when a switch is on. Hover an icon for its name, its current state and what it does. Number settings use small −/+ buttons; hold Shift for bigger steps.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.anvil: Star Anvil - tool on top, core below, press Upgrade: the tool rises one tier and keeps enchantments, name, charge and settings.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.anvil2: The base tools come from the crafting table: Netherite pickaxe, axe and shovel + 2 Stellar Steel make the drill; a Netherite sword + 2 Stellar Steel the blade; a bow + a Netherite Ingot + 2 Stellar Steel the bow.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.anvil3: The anvil also lists every effect with an on/off switch - and which tier unlocks the ones you don't have yet.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.blade: Stellar Blade - a sword that grows from 9 attack damage (Netherite) to 31 (Singularity).
scc.guide.stellar_gear.blade1: Red Dwarf - Red Harvest: Looting +1 and every kill heals half a heart.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.blade2: Yellow Star - Sun Flash: right-click blinds and slows enemies in front of you (8 blocks, 2,000 FE, 8 s).
scc.guide.stellar_gear.blade3: Blue Giant - Plasma Arc: every full swing - also into thin air - throws a plasma sickle through up to 3 enemies (about 20 blocks, 1,000 FE).
scc.guide.stellar_gear.blade4: Neutron Star - Gravity Strike: a full hit pulls enemies within 6 blocks to the target and slams flying ones down (4,000 FE, 6 s).
scc.guide.stellar_gear.blade5: Singularity - Time Stop: hold right-click for a second and release. Enemies within 10 blocks freeze for 5 s - no movement, no AI. Costs 1 Chronon (inventory or the bound network) and 20,000 FE, 60 s cooldown.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.blade6: Bosses (Wither, Ender Dragon, tag c:bosses) are only slowed: never blinded, pulled or frozen. Players, pets and villagers are never hit by the abilities.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.bow: Stellar Bow - a bow on FE, a little stronger with every tier.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.bow0: With FE it shoots plasma arrows: no arrows needed (100 FE per shot), fully drawn after 16 ticks (Singularity 11 - a normal bow needs 20), 6 to 9 damage at full draw plus Power. Plasma arrows never lie around - they vanish at the first block. Without FE it is a normal bow that shoots arrows from your inventory.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.bow1: Red Dwarf - Ember Shot: burning plasma arrows, and kills with the bow get Looting +1 (25 FE).
scc.guide.stellar_gear.bow2: Yellow Star - Solar Volley: a fully drawn shot fires 3 arrows in a fan, the side arrows hit for 60 % (150 FE).
scc.guide.stellar_gear.bow3: Blue Giant - Plasma Bolt: a fully drawn shot becomes a fast bolt without drop that passes through up to 3 creatures (500 FE).
scc.guide.stellar_gear.bow4: Neutron Star - Gravity Arrow: the impact pulls enemies within 5 blocks together and slams flying ones down (2,000 FE, 6 s).
scc.guide.stellar_gear.bow5: Singularity - Seeking Star: fully drawn arrows curve gently towards the nearest enemy ahead (200 FE).
scc.guide.stellar_gear.bow6: Plasma arrows hit like normal arrows (players only where PvP is on). Bolt, gravity and seeking never touch players, pets or villagers; bosses are only slowed. Enchanting: everything a bow takes (Power, Punch, Flame, Infinity, Unbreaking) - Unbreaking saves FE.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.bubble: Star Bubble - 4 from glass, amethyst and an ender pearl. A filled bubble shows what is inside; right-click a block to release the mob with everything it had. The bubble is empty again.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.chargewarn: When a piece of Stellar Gear you wear or hold drops below 10 % power - the Exo flight and the plasma shield simply stop without it - a short SCC notice with a soft chime tells you once. It warns again only after the piece was charged above 25 %. Turn it off under F7 - Stellar Gear low power warning.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.controls1: Sneak + right-click with the tool: the settings window - every effect on/off, hammer size and depth, Silk or Fortune.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.controls2: Right-click an antenna or controller: bind the tool to that network (drill drops, Chronon for the blade).
scc.guide.stellar_gear.controls3: Blade: right-click = Sun Flash, hold and release = Time Stop.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.controls4: The tooltip shows tier, charge and all effects; hold Shift to see what each one does.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.controls5: Worn Exo: the key "Stellar Exo settings" (unbound by default, set it in Controls) shows all worn pieces at once; "Gravity Boots on/off" switches the boots. The window has two tabs: Armor (worn pieces, flight and Star Wings) and Tools (every Stellar tool in your inventory, switched without holding it); each effect shows its power cost and each piece its live FE/t.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.cores: Star Cores - one per tier: 2 Stellar Steel and 4 star matter of that tier in the Star Forge (Sun Core, Blue Plasma, Neutronium and Dark Matter for the higher ones).
scc.guide.stellar_gear.drill: Stellar Drill - pickaxe, axe and shovel in one. Right-click does what an axe or a shovel would: strip logs, scrape and unwax copper, make paths, put out campfires - modded blocks included.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.drill1: Red Dwarf - Ember: ores become ingots, sand becomes glass (tag scc:stellar_autosmelt).
scc.guide.stellar_gear.drill2: Yellow Star - Hammer 3×3 (sneak = single block) and Sunpower: double speed in daylight under open sky. An outline shows exactly which blocks the hammer will take.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.drill3: Blue Giant - 5×5 and depth 1 or 3, Silk Touch / Fortune switch (Silk Touch pauses an enchanted Fortune, Fortune counts at least as III), Plasma Cutter: obsidian and ancient debris as fast as stone.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.drill4: Neutron Star - Network Link: right-click an antenna or controller to bind; drops go straight into storage while you are within its wireless range (antenna range upgrades count).
scc.guide.stellar_gear.drill5: Singularity - Black Hole Drill Head: a whole ore vein or tree at once, up to 64 blocks, 150 FE per block. The hammer also goes 7×7 (147 blocks at depth 3).
scc.guide.stellar_gear.drill6: Area and vein mining only take blocks the drill could mine by hand: never bedrock, never blocks with an inventory or a machine inside, never fluids - and claims are checked for every single block.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.ench: Enchanting: the drill takes everything a pickaxe, axe or shovel takes (Efficiency, Fortune, Silk Touch ...), the blade everything a sword takes (Sharpness, Smite, Bane of Arthropods, Looting, Fire Aspect, Knockback, Sweeping Edge) - at the enchanting table and with books on the anvil. Unbreaking saves power: level n divides every FE cost by n+1. Mending may go on but has nothing to repair.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.exo: Stellar Exo - helmet, chestplate, leggings and boots with Netherite protection plus the Star Hull, on FE instead of durability. Each piece: its Netherite piece + 2 Stellar Steel.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.exo0: Every piece is upgraded on its own in the Star Anvil. An effect works when the piece that carries it has reached the tier - the tooltip of each piece lists its effects.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.exo1: Leggings, Red Dwarf - Core Heat: no freezing (with Exo boots you also walk on powder snow), fire and lava damage cut to a quarter. Small warm sparks show it is on.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.exo2: Helmet, Yellow Star - Solar Skin: in daylight under open sky it slowly charges your worn armor and held Stellar tools, 20 up to 40 FE/t (Singularity) in total.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.exo3: Chestplate, Blue Giant - Plasma Shield: 3 charges, each fully blocks one hit (melee, projectile, explosion) with a blue flash. One charge back every 20 s for 2,000 FE; the charges are shown above the food bar. Not against /kill, the void, hunger, falling, fire or poison.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.exo4: Boots, Neutron Star - Gravity Boots: stand on walls and ceilings. Walk into a wall at least two blocks high and you step onto it - gravity, camera, controls and your hitbox turn with you: forward walks along the surface, jump pushes you off it. Walk into the next surface to switch, from the floor onto the wall, onto the ceiling and back down. Bump a ceiling while holding jump to flip onto it. Walk over an outer edge and you follow it around onto the next side of the block - the view turns with you, so looking straight ahead stays straight ahead; over the top of a wall you end up on top of it. Sneak to return to normal gravity. Mining, building and bows work in any direction. No fall damage, 2 FE per tick on a wall or ceiling. If turning upside down makes you dizzy: F7 → "Gravity Boots: turn the camera" off keeps the view upright.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.exo5: Chestplate, Singularity - Event Horizon: hostile projectiles within 5 blocks are swallowed (500 FE each), enemies close by are slowed slightly.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.exo6: Set bonus - Flight: only when all four pieces are Singularity. Creative-style flight for 50 FE per tick from the chestplate. No single piece can fly - three Singularity pieces and one Neutron Star piece do not.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.exo7: At 0 FE the armor keeps its full Netherite protection; the Star Hull and the effects stop. Charging works like the tools: Stellar Distributor with a Charging Module, or Charge gear on the Wireless Terminal (a quarter).
scc.guide.stellar_gear.exonv: Helmet, Red Dwarf - Night Vision: you see in the dark for 1 FE/t, without particles, icon or the flicker at the end. At 0 FE or switched off it fades; potions are left alone.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.exowings: Star Wings: put the Singularity chestplate and an Elytra into the Star Anvil and press Upgrade (the Elytra is used up). With the full Singularity set you can then switch between Creative flight and Elytra gliding - in the Exo window, on the Star Anvil or with the hotkey "Star Wings: switch flight mode". Gliding costs 10 FE/t and never wears out; the automatic boost (Off/Gentle/Medium/Strong) pushes you like a rocket for 60-200 FE/t more. Sneak pauses the boost. Out of power you glide on to the ground but cannot take off again.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.gadgets0: Helpers that run on the same power as the gear (250k FE, Stellar Distributor or Charge gear) and never break. Only the Star Shield has tiers.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.gauntlet: Gravity Gauntlet - right-click lifts a mob, an item or a loose block; it floats in front of you. Right-click again throws it.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.gauntlet1: Loose blocks: everything that falls like sand and gravel, and soft blocks like dirt and grass. A thrown block lands like sand.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.gauntlet2: Sneak + right-click pulls all items and XP within 10 blocks to you (1,000 FE, 2 s cooldown).
scc.guide.stellar_gear.gauntlet3: 500 FE per lift, 5 FE per tick while holding, at most 10 s. Mobs up to 100 health - never players, bosses, other players' pets or blocks with an inventory. Claims are checked like breaking a block.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.grenade: Gravity Grenade - throw it: where it lands, a tiny black hole pulls every mob within 5 blocks to the middle for 3 s. 4 per craft, stacks to 16.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.grenade1: No damage, no block damage, no fall damage for the pulled mobs. Never players, bosses or pets; in someone else's claim it fizzles.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.hull: Star Hull - every Exo piece absorbs damage while it has FE: 15, 30, 45, 60, 75% per tier, a full Singularity set absorbs everything. Never /kill or the void.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.lasso: Star Lasso - right-click a mob to catch it in an empty Star Bubble from your inventory.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.lasso1: Passive and neutral mobs up to 100 health (cows, horses, villagers, iron golems): 1,000 FE.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.lasso2: Hostile mobs up to 40 health (zombies, creepers, endermen), and only at half health or less: fight first, then catch. 5,000 FE.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.lasso3: Never players, bosses or other players' pets - your own pets are fine, so you can move with your dog. Not in someone else's claim.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.mod1: Stellar Modules - extras you choose yourself, on top of the fixed tier effects. Forged in the Star Forge from a vanilla item and two star matter of their tier.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.mod10: The window shows for every module what its level does ("+45% speed") and what it costs ("30 FE/s"), the free core load and the upkeep of the piece. Installing, removing and switching have their own sound and light.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.mod11: In the HUD a small bar shows your active modules with their level (gray: piece without FE). In the world Speed Boost leaves a star trail when sprinting and Jump Boost a ring when jumping. Both can be turned off in the SCC settings, the bar can move to any corner.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.mod2: Sneak + right-click the gear and press "Modules" (in the Exo window: the small ◈ button next to each piece). The piece floats as a hologram in the middle, its slots around it.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.mod3: Every module item is one level - install three Vitality modules for Vitality III. With the level bar you can turn it lower at any time, and switch each module off.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.mod4: A piece has tier + 1 slots (Netherite 1 up to Singularity 6) and a core load budget (4 up to 26). Every active level costs core load - you cannot have everything at once. Higher tiers also allow higher levels.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.mod5: Helmet: Clarity, Detox, Water Breathing, Star Sight. Chestplate: Vitality (up to +10 hearts), Regeneration. Leggings: Speed Boost, Jump Boost. Boots: Step Assist, Water Walking.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.mod6: Blade: Star Edge, Armor Breaker, Critical Strike, Looting. Bow: Power, Quick Draw, Looting. Drill: Fortune, Efficiency, Trash Filter, Starlight.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.mod7: Looting and Fortune reach the maximum Apothic Enchanting allows (otherwise III). Fortune works with the Silk/Fortune switch: on Silk Touch it rests.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.mod8: Modules come out of the inventory - or out of the network the piece is linked to. Remove one level again with the red button or a right-click on its slot.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.mod9: Quick menu (%s, set it under Controls): a ring with the modules of all worn and held pieces - click switches a module on or off, no inventory needed.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.modtable: What the modules do - at level I and at their top level:
scc.guide.stellar_gear.omni: Stellar Drill Upgrade: Omni Mining - put the drill on top and the upgrade in the core slot of the Star Anvil (any tier). From then on the drill mines every block with full drops, whatever mining level it needs: Allthemodium, Vibranium and Unobtainium, Aurichalcum and Adamantite, and the ores of every other mod. Hammer, vein, Ember, Silk Touch/Fortune and Network Link all work with it.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.omni2: The recipe depends on the modpack: 4 Unobtainium Ingots when Allthemodium is installed, otherwise 4 Aurichalcum Ingots if the pack has them (FTB Evolution), otherwise 4 Netherite Ingots - plus 2 Stellar Steel, 2 Neutronium and a Star Core (Neutron Star). The guide and JEI/EMI show the active one.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.omni3: Pack makers can replace it - the recipe IDs are scc:omni_mining_upgrade/unobtainium, scc:omni_mining_upgrade/aurichalcum and scc:omni_mining_upgrade/netherite. Bedrock, barriers and protected claims stay off-limits.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.orbit: Orbit Formation - carries up to 4 satellites (6 with an expanded pedestal). Anywhere in your inventory (or a Curios charm slot) they orbit you and work. Right-click: on/off; right-click an antenna or controller: link it to the network.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.orbit1: Collector: pulls items and XP to you - 6 blocks with one, up to 16. Linked to a network (like the Drill), items go straight into storage.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.orbit2: Gunner: star bolts at hostile mobs - 2 hearts each (+50% against undead), every 1.5 s with one, 150 FE per shot. From strength 2 a bolt pierces a second target.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.orbit3: Healer: half a heart every 3 s with one, at best every second - 400 FE each. From strength 2 it removes a harmful effect every 30 s, from 3 it adds 2 hearts of absorption.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.orbit4: Lantern: an invisible light at your head (level 11 to 15), nearby enemies glow and take 15% more damage from you, and no monsters spawn around you.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.orbit5: Neighbours: the same role next to each other in the ring gets +35% per neighbour (the line between them glows on the pedestal).
scc.guide.stellar_gear.orbit6: Power: the formation's own 250k FE first, then a worn Stellar Exo chestplate. Without power the satellites keep orbiting but do nothing.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.orbit_combo: Combos (different roles next to each other, purple line on the pedestal): Gunner + Lantern - bolts make targets glow and hit glowing ones 25% harder. Healer + Shield - the shield recharges 40% faster.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.orbit_comet: Comet Satellite - up to +40% speed (8% per strength) and step assist (walk up full blocks), a star trail while sprinting. 20 FE per second.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.orbit_expansion: Constellation Expansion I and II - right-click a Constellation Pedestal to unlock satellite slot 5, then 6. The pedestal keeps its slots when you break it, and the formation keeps its satellites everywhere.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.orbit_full: Full formation: at least 4 satellites and no role twice - every role works 20% stronger.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.orbit_magic: Magic Ward Satellite - 15% less magic damage per strength, at most 60% (server config). Works on every damage type tagged as magic, so spells from Ars Nouveau, Iron's Spells and other magic mods; with Iron's Spells it also raises its spell resistance. Only craftable when a magic mod is installed.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.orbit_repair: Repair Satellite - every damaged item you wear or hold gets 1 durability back every 2 s (divided by its strength), 40 FE per point.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.orbit_shield: Shield Satellite - catches one incoming projectile every 8 s (divided by its strength), 300 FE each. From strength 2: 2 hearts of absorption that refill slowly.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.pedestal: Constellation Pedestal - formation in the middle, satellites in the ring around it. The satellites live in the formation; the pedestal is just the workbench.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.planet: Planetarium - the control centre of your Stellar Gear. Three planets circle a tiny sun under a golden dome.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.planet1: Right-click: everything you carry with a charge - tier, FE, every effect with its switch, the Orbit Formation with its satellites (on/off) and your Little Stars (sit/follow, call).
scc.guide.stellar_gear.planet2: Only the player who placed it can open it. It switches what you carry; stored gear stays as it is.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.planet3: Sky projection: at night or in a dark room the Planetarium casts the five sky objects, their orbits and a few stars onto ceiling and walls - where they really stand in the sky right now, slowly turning.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.planet4: Sneak + right-click switches the projection on and off; a redstone signal switches it off while it is applied. F7 → Planetarium sky projection switches it off on your screen.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.pocket: Stellar Pocket - a tool bag for your belt or charm slot (Curios) or simply your inventory.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.pocket1: Press G (rebindable under Controls): tap to put the tool in your hand back into the pocket; hold, point at a tool and let go to take it - the tool you held takes its place.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.pocket2: With an empty hand a tap keeps the wheel open: click a tool or press 1-9. "Open pocket" in the wheel or right-clicking the pocket shows all slots.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.pocket3: Tools, weapons, gadgets and Stellar Gear fit - also those of other mods: anything with durability, items tagged as tools, battery-powered gadgets, portable crafting stations (Crafting on a Stick) and SCC's own tools (Network Tool, Wrench, Design Brush, Wireless Terminals, Wormhole Remote ...). No blocks, armor, food or containers. 9 slots; at a Smithing Table with a Star Shard and a Stellar Steel Ingot it grows to 18, then 27, and the tools stay inside.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.pocket4: The tools travel inside the pocket itself: hand it to a friend and they come along; if it is ever destroyed, they drop out.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.pocket5: Tap G while looking at a block and the pocket hands you its best tool for that block: one that really gets a drop out of it, on ores the one with the most Fortune (Silk Touch only if nothing else works), otherwise the fastest. The tool you held goes into the pocket. If it already is the best, the tap puts it away as usual.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.power1: Each block costs 100 FE, each hit 100 FE. The abilities cost more (see below).
scc.guide.stellar_gear.power2: Full speed charging at a Stellar Distributor with a Charging Module.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.power3: Wirelessly with Charge gear on the Wireless Terminal: a quarter of the speed - enough in the field, the Distributor is faster.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.power4: FE = storage, FE/t = charge rate at the Distributor (wireless a quarter), Drill = mining speed, Blade = attack damage.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.resonance: Chronon Resonance - at the Star Anvil a blade gets +1 attack damage per resonance. The n-th costs n Chronon; the server sets the limit (default 50, chrononResonanceMax).
scc.guide.stellar_gear.safe1: Without power nothing breaks, but the drill gets slow, the blade hits only half as hard, the bow needs normal arrows again and all effects stop.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.safe2: The gear has its own ladder: Netherite → Stellar Steel → Star Cores from the Star Forge - not the lens prisms.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.satellites: Satellites - one per role, each from iron, amethyst, redstone and a role part: hopper, dispenser, glistering melon, glowstone, shield, anvil, feather or lapis block.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.shield: Star Shield - blocks like a shield and never breaks. Every block flashes with light.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.shield1: Star Mirror: projectiles that hit the raised shield from the front fly back where you look (250 FE each). Arrows, fireballs, snowballs, tridents.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.shield2: Tiers at the Star Anvil like Drill and Blade: Ember Rim (attackers burn), Guide Beam (back to the shooter), Plasma Push (knock back), Dense Mirror (arrows x2), Nova Flash (enemies in front glow and slow down).
scc.guide.stellar_gear.shield3: Without power it still blocks like a normal shield - only the effects stay quiet. Switches: Star Anvil or Planetarium.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.star: Little Star - a tame companion. Right-click a block with the item: it appears, floats above your shoulder and follows you.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.star1: It glows (light follows it), collects items within 6 blocks and hands them to you - as long as you are within 24 blocks.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.star2: It never fights and cannot be hurt. Far away it jumps to you; it climbs back out of the void on its own.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.star3: Right-click: sit / follow. Design Brush in hand: right-click paints it (or paint the item in the off hand). Sneak + right-click with an empty hand: back into the item.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.star4: Night light: in caves and at night it glows brighter and throws warm light onto floor and walls - without placing any blocks. With Sodium Dynamic Lights or LambDynamicLights it lights up the area for real. F7 → Little Star night light. Servers can bring back the old invisible light blocks (they stop mobs spawning) with /scc littleStarLightBlocks on.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.steel: Stellar Steel Ingot - a Netherite Ingot and 4 Red Dwarf Ember in the Star Forge. The base of everything here.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.sun: Mini Sun - place it on a block, or throw it: where it lands it floats up and stays. Right-click: on/off.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.sun1: Light 15 at the sun and a ring of invisible lights around it - the whole area is bright, not just one block.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.sun2: No natural monster spawns within 16 blocks (spawners stay, like with torches). Crops, saplings, sugar cane and co. within 8 blocks grow about 50% faster.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.sun3: 10 FE/t while lit. Own 250k FE buffer - full, it shines about 20 minutes on its own. Refills from an SCC cable next to it, from other mods' cables, or as an item at the Stellar Distributor; the charge stays in the item when you break it.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.sun_redstone: A redstone signal switches it off - with an inverted daylight detector it only shines at night and saves its power during the day.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.what: Stellar Gear - a drill, a blade, a bow and the Stellar Exo armor from Netherite upwards. Each star tier adds one fixed effect, and every effect can be switched off.
scc.guide.stellar_gear.what2: They run on FE instead of durability: at 0 FE they never break, they just get slow and the effects stop.
scc.guide.storage.compress: Auto-compress: in the Calculator Controller, tab Rules, the button with the matter symbol. The network then packs nuggets into ingots and ingots into blocks (and every other 9 or 4 item recipe that can be crafted back, mod items included) - a few stacks per second in the background. Choose whether everything goes to the highest tier or 64 / 256 of each lower tier stay. Whoever needs ingots - you, an order, a Transfer Calculator - gets them anyway: blocks are split on demand. Items reserved for running orders are never packed. Pack makers exclude items with the item tag scc:no_compress.
scc.guide.storage.connector: Attaches exactly one container to the network. Anything that offers an inventory works: chests, barrels, shulker boxes, drawers, modded storage. Point it at a tank instead and the fluid inside belongs to the network too, so machine recipes that need water can draw from it.
scc.guide.storage.creative: A storage that never runs out: whatever is in its filter is available without limit, and anything put in disappears. For building and testing - creative only, and deliberately not craftable.
scc.guide.storage.drain: Every own item storage block has an "Empty out" button in its window: it moves everything into the rest of the network, so a storage block can be swapped without losing what is in it.
scc.guide.storage.filter1: Every connector can decide what it lets in. Click an item from your cursor into one of the 27 filter slots (three rows) and only that item goes into this container. Scroll over the slot to switch to one of the item's tags - c:ores, minecraft:logs - so an ore chest takes every ore of every mod without listing them.
scc.guide.storage.filter2: You can also type a tag or a pattern into the field above the slots: c:ores/* or *ingots*, with * standing for anything. Whitelist lets in only what is listed, blacklist everything except.
scc.guide.storage.filter3: The filter only decides what the network puts in. Taking out is never filtered, and whatever is already inside stays visible - a filter is not a way to hide things.
scc.guide.storage.flow1: Every connector has an access mode.
scc.guide.storage.flow2: Import + export - the default. The network reads from it and puts into it.
scc.guide.storage.flow3: Import only - a source. The network takes from it and never puts anything back. Right for a furnace output chest, or a drop chest you only want drained.
scc.guide.storage.flow4: Export only - a destination. The network fills it and never takes back. Its contents drop out of the network entirely, so no order can plan with them. Right for a supply chest that has to stay stocked.
scc.guide.storage.fluids1: A connector on a tank can be locked to whatever is inside right now, so a mixed setup never ends up with the wrong liquid in the wrong tank. In the terminal, left-clicking a fluid fills a bucket from storage.
scc.guide.storage.interface: The network as an ordinary chest, for everything SCC does not know. Pipes, belts, hoppers and machines see nine slots: a slot without a template swallows whatever is put in, a slot with one is kept filled from storage so anything can help itself.
scc.guide.storage.interface2: This is the one block that connects SCC to another mod without SCC having to know that mod.
scc.guide.storage.interface3: Next to a Create Schematicannon the Interface shows the cannon the whole network instead of its nine slots: the cannon finds every block in storage and takes what the schematic needs - nothing has to be set as a template. It only takes, it never stores. Hoppers and pipes on the same Interface still see the nine slots. Modpacks can add more blocks to the block tag scc:sees_whole_network.
scc.guide.storage.interface4: Chemicals work like fluids: whatever a Mekanism pipe sends in goes into storage, and a chemical dragged from JEI or EMI onto a template can be taken out by pipes there.
scc.guide.storage.monitor: A panel showing the stock of a single item, large enough to read in passing - and it works like a drawer, so you rarely need a terminal standing next to it.
scc.guide.storage.monitor2: Left-click takes a stack, right-click with an empty hand takes one item, right-click with something in hand puts it in, and sneaking while you do that adds everything of that kind from your inventory. The first thing you put into an empty panel becomes what it watches; sneak + right-click with an empty hand clears it again. Breaking it needs a sneak first - otherwise the hit would take a stack out instead. Below the number it shows the balance of the last minute.
scc.guide.storage.monitor3: Right-click the panel with a battery - anything that carries FE - and it stops watching an item and shows the power of the whole network instead: how much is stored, how full that is, and whether the network is gaining or losing power right now, in FE/t. Green means it is filling up, red means it is draining, and the number tells you how fast. Sneak + right-click with an empty hand puts it back to nothing.
scc.guide.storage.monitor4: Fluids too: right-click the panel with a filled bucket or any fluid container (tank, cell) - it pours it into the network and from then on shows that fluid, in mB or B (buckets), with its balance per minute. Right-click with an empty bucket or container to fill it from the network; left-click or an empty hand takes an empty bucket from storage and hands it to you filled.
scc.guide.storage.monitor5: Several Storage Monitors side by side on one wall, facing the same way, join into one big screen (up to 8×8) that shows the item and its amount large. Clicking any block of it acts on the whole screen, and the wrench switches 2D/3D for all of it.
scc.guide.storage.own: Storage the network brings along - no chest behind it, the block is the storage. Place it on a cable and it is part of the network at once: priority, access mode and filter work exactly as on the connector, because it is the same block underneath with one difference - it reaches into itself instead of into the container in front.
scc.guide.storage.owncarry: Break one and the contents travel inside the item, like a shulker box. Place it again and everything is back. That is not a convenience - the top tier can hold tens of thousands of stacks, and pouring those onto the floor would be a crash, not a move.
scc.guide.storage.ownchemical: And the same for Mekanism's chemicals. It behaves like the fluid storage - one tank per chemical, the tier says how many tanks and how much each holds - but the ladder starts higher, at 64 B per tank, because that is where Mekanism's own tanks start. Mekanism pipes connect to it on every side. Without Mekanism installed the block still keeps whatever is inside it; it just takes nothing new.
scc.guide.storage.ownenergy: And the same for energy. FE becomes a resource of the network like any other. Getting power in is the ordinary way: run a cable from your generator straight into an Energy Storage - it takes FE on every side like any battery does. A Storage Connector pointed at a battery you already have counts too. Machines then draw from the network through the FE switch on a Processing Calculator, and a Transfer Calculator with FE on pushes it into anything else. Note that pulling FE back out of a machine usually does not work, and that is not a setting: a generator hands energy out, a consumer only takes it in - that is how Forge energy is built.
scc.guide.storage.ownfluid: The same for fluids. Every tier says how many tanks it has and how much each holds; a new fluid takes the next free tank, and a fluid that fills its tank simply carries on in the next free one.
scc.guide.storage.owngauge: A gauge runs along the bottom of every storage block and lights up in the colour of its tier, so you can read a wall of storage at a glance instead of clicking through it. Up close it shows the exact level and a light runs along it; from further away it steps in fifths. Singularity storage never fills up, so it shows a light running end to end instead of a level. A comparator next to any storage block reads the exact level.
scc.guide.storage.ownsoul: And one for souls from Industrial Foregoing Souls. A Storage Connector or Transfer Calculator on top of a Soul Laser Base brings its souls into the network; Soul Pipes and Soul Surges get them back from an SCC Interface. Crafted only when Industrial Foregoing Souls is installed.
scc.guide.storage.ownsource: And one for Source from Ars Nouveau. Ars machines and relays treat it like a Source Jar, but every block shares the whole network's Source - place one next to your Enchanting Apparatus and it draws from all of them. A Storage Connector facing a Source Jar adds that jar to the pool. Crafted only when Ars Nouveau is installed.
scc.guide.storage.owntable: What each tier holds on this server - the server config can change these limits (the storage... entries):
scc.guide.storage.owntiers: Six tiers, each built from the one below. Counted in items, not in slots - one sword costs one, sixty-four ingots cost sixty-four: 4,000 items, then 16,000, 64,000, 256,000, 1,000,000 - and Singularity, which has no limit at all. Fluids and energy climb the same ladder. The infinite one is deliberately kept out of the network's fill gauge: it cannot fill up, so a percentage would say nothing.
scc.guide.storage.prio1: Higher priority is filled first, and only what does not fit moves on to the next connector. Negative numbers work too. Use it to keep one chest as the overflow and everything else tidy.
scc.guide.storage.prio2: Taking out has its own number if you want one. "Take from this chest, but never store in it" is store -10, take +10; leave it on "same" and one number governs both, as before.
scc.guide.storage.subnet1: A small automation can have its own controller and still use the main network - without both turning into one network:
scc.guide.storage.subnet2: Put an Interface on the main network and point the front of a Storage Connector of the small network at it. The small network then sees the main network's whole storage, like an AE2 Storage Bus on an ME Interface - filter and import/export decide which part it may take or store.
scc.guide.storage.subnet3: A Transfer Calculator pointing at that Interface pushes into the main network or takes what the Interface hands out. Neither of them joins the two networks.
scc.guide.storage.subnet4: The main network does not see the small network's chests and gives no orders to its machines. The player who placed the Interface needs the Take right on the main network.
scc.guide.storage.void1: A connector can delete what no longer fits instead of letting it clog the network - for gravel, cobble and stone. The switch sits next to the access direction.
scc.guide.storage.void2: It only works with a whitelist that has at least one slot filled. Without one it would delete everything the network has no room for, so it stays inactive and says so.
scc.guide.terminals.crafting: The same terminal with a 3x3 grid attached. The grid belongs to the block, not to the window: what you put in stays in, survives closing, and is there for everyone who opens it. On a server that matters - a grid that emptied itself when one player closed the screen would look broken to the next one. If several recipes fit the same ingredients, a small button next to the result lets you pick what the grid crafts; with Polymorph installed, Polymorph's own button does it.
scc.guide.terminals.hidden1: Shift + middle-click on a craftable item in the terminal hides it from the list - handy for things you never want to build. Only the craftable entry goes away: what is in storage always shows.
scc.guide.terminals.hidden2: F7 > Hidden items lists everything you have hidden, with a search field. Click a line or its Show again button to bring that one item back; Show all brings back the whole list after asking once. Items from a mod you have removed stay in the list with their id, so you can clear them too.
scc.guide.terminals.history1: Hover an item in a terminal: below its name you see the trend ("+1.2K/h" green, "-300/h" red) and a small chart of the last 24 hours. Hold Shift for the last 2 hours. So you see at a glance whether a farm is running or something is draining.
scc.guide.terminals.history2: The network records a point every 5 minutes, only for items that change or that someone looks at - also fine in a base with 50,000 kinds. Hours of play time count; while the network is unloaded the chart has a gap. Turn it off under F7; server owners use /scc stockHistory off.
scc.guide.terminals.hole: Black hole as a trash can
scc.guide.terminals.hole1: If a Stellar Cradle with a black hole is in the network, you can throw any item into it from the terminal: hover over the item and press Delete (rebindable), choose 1, a stack, all or a number, and confirm. With an item on the cursor, click the black hole button in the toolbar menu.
scc.guide.terminals.hole2: Thrown items count as food: same FE per item, same Chronon. Items reserved by running orders stay. Enchanted, named or filled items need a second click. Needs the right "take out" ("put in" for items from your inventory).
scc.guide.terminals.monitor: Every calculator on the network on one panel: which one is working, which is idle, which one is the bottleneck. It measures load over the last minute instead of showing a snapshot, because every machine is briefly idle between two runs and a snapshot tells you nothing. The button at the top opens the network report - the first thing to look at when an item says it cannot be built.
scc.guide.terminals.order1: Pick an amount and the window shows what comes out of storage, what has to be crafted, and what is missing - all before you commit to anything. The tree button opens the full path the order would take: every recipe, every machine, every step.
scc.guide.terminals.order2: Max sets the largest amount the stock you have can actually produce.
scc.guide.terminals.order3: Right-click any line in the tree to choose which recipe the calculator has to use for that item - the pin marks lines you have fixed. Automatic hands the choice back. A fixed recipe is fixed: if it cannot be built, the tree says so instead of quietly taking another route. The swap button at the end of a line with several recipes opens the same choice. Your choice is saved and used for every later order of that item - like a single pattern in AE2.
scc.guide.terminals.order4: Items that come in variants - chests in every wood, coloured blocks - show two arrows next to the name. They switch between all the variants you can build. If the one you clicked can't be built but another can, the window picks that one for you.
scc.guide.terminals.order5: Middle-click a line in the tree to choose which option an ingredient uses - which wood, which chest - with your stock shown next to each. Automatic hands the choice back.
scc.guide.terminals.order6: In that recipe choice, click the machine on a recipe card to choose the machine for every recipe of that type - for example all Smelting recipes on your Furnaces instead of an Alloy Smelter. Each click takes the next machine on the network; after the last one it is automatic again. A gold frame marks your choice, and only that machine gets those recipes. Automatic goes by the Processing Calculator priority first, then prefers machines made for the recipe type.
scc.guide.terminals.orderkeys: In the order window, hover the ordered item or an ingredient and press R or U - JEI or EMI shows its recipes or uses, as in AE2.
scc.guide.terminals.recentorders1: Three dots - Recently ordered lists your last 10 orders with amount. A click opens the order window with item and amount filled in, Shift + click orders again right away (if it can be planned), right-click removes an entry. The row above the storage shows the same items. The list is kept per player on the server.
scc.guide.terminals.recentsort: Sorting "Recently changed" (three dots - Sort, or the sort tab): whatever was just stored or taken out stands at the top - the harvest of a farm, the loot after Store inventory. It follows the changes your game has seen since it was started.
scc.guide.terminals.rights1: On a server a network needs an owner, and that is whoever placed the Calculator Controller. Everybody else gets exactly the rights the owner hands out:
scc.guide.terminals.rights2: Take - may take items and fluids out of storage.
scc.guide.terminals.rights3: Put - may put items and fluids into storage.
scc.guide.terminals.rights5: Build - may open and change the blocks of the network.
scc.guide.terminals.rights6: The Security Terminal is where you hand them out. Put it on a cable like any other wall panel, right-click it, type a name and click the four boxes. A player who is offline right now still shows up in the list and can still be removed.
scc.guide.terminals.rights7: None of it does anything until an operator switches rights on with /scc set security on. The terminal says so in its top line.
scc.guide.terminals.search1: iron block - words in any order
scc.guide.terminals.searchfilter: The funnel next to it opens the filters: only craftable, only in storage, fluids, chemicals or a single mod. The funnel lights up while a filter is on, and the choice stays after a restart.
scc.guide.terminals.searchworld: The beam button at the end of the search field shows where everything from your search is stored: every storage that holds some of it lights up through walls for 20 seconds, the fullest ones in gold. For a single item, Alt + click does the same.
scc.guide.terminals.security: Hands out the rights of the network - who may take, put, order and build. Only the owner can open it.
scc.guide.terminals.stocktip1: With a linked Wireless Terminal in your inventory or a Curios slot, the tooltip of every item - in your inventory, in chests, in JEI and EMI - shows "In network: 1,234". Buckets and tanks show the fluid in the network. The number comes from the network behind your terminal, only within its range and only if you may take things from it.
scc.guide.terminals.stocktip2: The first look at an item shows the line a moment later - SCC only asks for the item under your mouse, never for the whole list. Turn it off under F7 - Network stock in item tooltips; server owners switch it off with /scc stockTooltips off.
scc.guide.terminals.storagewarn1: When the storage of a network reaches 90 % and again when it is full, every player with access who stands near one of its terminals or carries a wireless terminal linked to it gets a short notice with a sound - items and SCC fluid storage count separately. In the terminal header a yellow (red when full) symbol appears; its tooltip lists items, SCC tanks and SCC energy. The next notice comes only after the level has dropped below 85 %, so a storage that hovers around the line does not keep calling.
scc.guide.terminals.storagewarn2: Turn the notices off for yourself under F7 - Storage warnings (the symbol stays). Server owners change the line with /scc storageWarnPercent 95 or switch it off with /scc storageWarnings off.
scc.guide.terminals.storeinv: Store inventory (in the menu behind the three dots): everything in your main inventory goes into the network with one click. Hotbar, armor, off-hand and wireless terminals stay with you; what does not fit stays in your inventory.
scc.guide.terminals.terminal: Shows everything in the network in one grid. Click an item to take a stack, right-click to take half of it; click a craftable one to open the order window. With something on the cursor, a click on the grid puts the whole stack in and a right-click puts in one item at a time. Ctrl+middle-click answers why something cannot be built, and Ctrl+Shift+right-click blocks a recipe for good.
scc.guide.terminals.toolbar1: The column of buttons on the left of the terminal holds only what you use all the time: sorting, categories, craftable items, only with ingredients, search sync and the job overview. Everything else sits in the menu behind the three dots, with icon and name: re-scan, stop jobs, order lists, notifications, remember search, the recently ordered row, hidden items, window scale and the SCC settings. When the recipe catalogue needs a re-scan, the three dots blink.
scc.guide.terminals.toolbar2: Right-click an entry in the menu to pin it to the bar; right-click a button on the bar to put it back into the menu. Your choice is saved on your client and applies to every terminal. If the bar runs out of room on a small screen, the last pinned buttons move into the menu instead of opening a second column.
scc.guide.terminals.toolbar3: In a wireless terminal one radio button collects what only matters there: Keep in inventory, Magnet (with its state), the Controller view and the two middle-click switches.
scc.guide.terminals.toolbar4: Your last orders sit as a row at the top of the grid, above the pinned items: click one to order it again, right-click removes it. The menu switches the row off if you would rather have the space for storage.
scc.guide.terminals.wall: Both terminals also come as a small panel that sits on the cable itself, the way AE2 does it: right-click the side of a cable with one and it moves in, keeping every connection the cable had. Same screen, same network. The panel is twelve pixels across, so a facade over the cable leaves a rim around it and the screen still looks out of the wall. A panel that moved into a cable keeps that cable inside it: break the panel and the cable drops with it, and the wrench leaves it lying instead. A panel placed straight onto a machine never had one, so it gives none back.
scc.guide.terminals.window1: Every SCC window can be dragged by its title bar. Dragging pins it, so it opens in that spot from then on - handy when a recipe view or a map wants the middle of the screen too. The pin in the top right corner shows it: click to unpin and the window goes back to the centre, click again to send it back where it was. Right-click the title bar forgets the spot entirely.
scc.guide.terminals.window2: Both terminals also resize: drag the grip in the bottom right corner to set how many columns and rows of storage you see - 9 to 18 wide, 3 to 12 tall on the plain terminal. The player inventory centres itself under the grid. An outline shows the new size while you drag; let go and the terminal reopens at that size.
scc.guide.terminals.window3: Every window resizes: drag the grip in the bottom right corner up or down. That sets Minecraft's own GUI scale while the window is open and puts it back when you close it - so text, items and the mouse all scale with it, which is the one thing a private magnifier cannot do. On the terminals the grip changes rows and columns instead; hold Ctrl there to set the scale.
scc.guide.tiers.breaking1: The Breaking Calculator uses the same ladder, with its own numbers: more blocks per run and more Fortune on top of the tool.
scc.guide.tiers.breaking2: Chronon Overdrive (Singularity only): switch it on in the window and, while there is Chronon in the network, the calculator speeds up step by step to the top speed below. Each step costs Chronon per second; without Chronon it falls back one step per second. All numbers here come from the server settings (breakBlocks..., breakTicks..., overdrive...) - change them with /scc <setting> <value> or in config/scc-server.json and /scc reloadconfig.
scc.guide.tiers.ladder1: Every tiered block climbs the same star ladder: Basic, Red Dwarf, Yellow Star, Blue Giant, Neutron Star and Singularity. A higher tier works faster and holds more jobs at once, and adds range to the network on top.
scc.guide.tiers.ladder2: Basic is crafted at the table. Every tier above it is forged in the Star Forge, from the block one tier below and the star matter of the new tier. Neutron Star is twenty times as fast as Basic; Singularity adds a special power per block (see the Singularity chapter).
scc.guide.tiers.stones1: Upgrade stones raise a block that is already placed: right-click it and it becomes the next tier, keeping all its settings. Stones are forged too - a redstone block and the matter of the tier. The Calculator Controller can fit them across the whole network.
scc.guide.tiers.stones2: The shortcut stones (Basic to Yellow Star and further) are crafted from the single-step stones, so you still need every step in between.
scc.guide.tips.f.alt: Transfer Calculator: Alt + scroll matches a whole tag, Shift + right-click: exactly this item or any of its kind.
scc.guide.tips.f.deny: Shift + click a filter slot: switch it between allow and exclude.
scc.guide.tips.f.fluid: Fluids: drag them in from JEI or EMI, or click with a filled bucket.
scc.guide.tips.f.scroll: Scroll over a filter slot (Storage Connector and others): switch to one of the item's tags.
scc.guide.tips.f.slot: Filter slot: click with an item on the cursor to set it, right-click clears it.
scc.guide.tips.f.text: Type a tag or a pattern into the filter field: c:ores/*, *ingots*.
scc.guide.tips.g.bind: Drill with the Network effect: right-click an antenna or controller - drops go into storage.
scc.guide.tips.g.blade: Stellar Blade: right-click Sun Flash, hold right-click 1 s and release: Time Stop.
scc.guide.tips.g.exo: %s: Stellar Exo window (armor and tools), %s: Gravity Boots on/off.
scc.guide.tips.g.gauntlet: Gravity Gauntlet: Sneak + right-click pulls items and XP within 10 blocks to you.
scc.guide.tips.g.pocket: %s: Stellar Pocket - tap puts the tool away (looking at a block: the best tool for it), hold to pick.
scc.guide.tips.g.settings: Sneak + right-click with a Stellar tool: its settings window.
scc.guide.tips.g.shift: Hold Shift over a Stellar item: what each effect does.
scc.guide.tips.g.wings: %s: Star Wings - switch between Creative flight and gliding.
scc.guide.tips.intro: Hotkeys, click combinations and hidden shortcuts at a glance. Keys shown in colour follow your own settings under Options > Controls.
scc.guide.tips.k.anim: %s / %s: Star Forge and Harvester animations / sounds on/off.
scc.guide.tips.k.hole: %s over an item in the terminal: throw it into the black hole (asks first; needs a Stellar Cradle with a black hole).
scc.guide.tips.k.job: %s: details of the last reported order, also after its notice is gone.
scc.guide.tips.k.lock: %s: lock a hotbar slot (in a window: the slot under the mouse) - middle-click pick never empties it.
scc.guide.tips.k.open: %s: open the calculator - over an item in a window, straight with that item.
scc.guide.tips.k.settings: %s: SCC settings - designs, sounds, notices, hidden items.
scc.guide.tips.k.unbound: Some keys are unbound by default - set them under Options > Controls, category SCC.
scc.guide.tips.k.wireless: %s: open the wireless terminal, %s: the wireless crafting terminal.
scc.guide.tips.m.auto: Side configuration: click next mode, right-click back. Auto button: Shift + click turns every side off, Ctrl + click moves every side one step.
scc.guide.tips.m.batch: Batch field: click to type, Shift + click doubles, right-click halves, scroll ±1 (Shift 8, Ctrl 64).
scc.guide.tips.m.custom: Custom recipe editor: middle-click a field to type its amount (Enter or a click elsewhere applies, Esc cancels); Shift + middle-click an ingredient: used up / stays in the machine.
scc.guide.tips.m.flow: Recipe flow (beam button in the custom recipe editor): click an ingredient, then a block on the map; drag it into another wave; scroll over it changes the target, right-click resets it. Switches: left/right click or scroll, Shift for bigger steps.
scc.guide.tips.m.machine: Right-click the machine icon: choose the machine and its recipes yourself.
scc.guide.tips.m.module: Empty module slot: click inserts or orders, Ctrl + click orders right away; Shift + click takes a module out.
scc.guide.tips.m.overview: Machines (terminal menu): click highlights the machine in the world, right-click opens its order.
scc.guide.tips.m.ports: Network Tool: Shift + right-click a Processing Calculator, then faces of other blocks - extra ports for multiblock machines.
scc.guide.tips.m.requester: Requester: click the target to type it, scroll ±1 (Shift 16, Ctrl 64); order size: right-click or scroll; the play/pause button left of the item switches a row, right-click clears it.
scc.guide.tips.m.steps: Number buttons and -/+: hold Shift (and Ctrl) for bigger steps.
scc.guide.tips.m.tree: Order tree: right-click a line to choose its recipe, middle-click to choose the variant (which wood, which chest).
scc.guide.tips.m.upgrade: Empty upgrade or card slot (Stellar Distributor, Network Antenna, Star Quarry, Sky Harvester ...): click inserts one from storage or inventory, Shift + click as many as fit (e.g. 8 Range Upgrades). What is missing opens the order window with that amount filled in - everything you order goes in when it is done, up to the slot limit; the rest stays in storage.
scc.guide.tips.o.brush: Design Brush: Shift + right-click a block copies its design.
scc.guide.tips.o.dist: Network Tool: Shift + right-click a Stellar Distributor, then blocks - it supplies only those (Linked mode).
scc.guide.tips.o.monitor: Storage Monitor: sneak while putting in adds everything of that kind; Sneak + right-click with an empty hand clears it.
scc.guide.tips.o.nettool: Network Tool: right-click shows what a block hangs on; Shift + right-click into the air stops linking.
scc.guide.tips.o.observatory: Stellar Observatory: right-click shows bottlenecks, suggestions, history and a map of your network; the hologram above it shows the last hour.
scc.guide.tips.o.wrench: Wrench: right-click turns, Shift + right-click takes a block down with its contents; hold %s for the wrench menu.
scc.guide.tips.t.amount: Amount fields understand shorthand and maths: 12k, 1.5m, 3*64, 3x64+10.
scc.guide.tips.t.block: Ctrl + Shift + right-click: block a recipe - the item is then only taken from storage, never built.
scc.guide.tips.t.carry: Item on the cursor: click stores the stack, right-click one item; a full bucket is poured into the tanks.
scc.guide.tips.t.chart: Hover an item: stock trend of the last 24 hours, hold Shift for the last 2 hours.
scc.guide.tips.t.dbl: Shift + double-click an item in your inventory: every stack of that kind goes into the network.
scc.guide.tips.t.drag: Shift + drag across items: each one goes into your inventory as a stack. Shift + scroll over an item: down takes one, up puts one back; over your inventory: down stores one, up takes one more.
scc.guide.tips.t.funnel: The funnel next to the search: filters - craftable, in storage, fluids, chemicals, one mod.
scc.guide.tips.t.history: Up / Down arrow in the search field: your earlier searches.
scc.guide.tips.t.jei: Crafting Terminal: hold Ctrl and click the "+" in JEI or EMI - the grid is filled and missing ingredients are ordered; they drop into the grid when done.
scc.guide.tips.t.locate: Alt + click: show where an item is stored, through walls.
scc.guide.tips.t.menu: The three dots: Network check, Machines, order lists, Store inventory, black hole and more. Right-click an entry to pin it to the bar.
scc.guide.tips.t.middle: Middle-click: order, even if some are in stock. Shift + middle-click: hide a craftable item. Ctrl + middle-click: why can it (not) be built?
scc.guide.tips.t.pin: Shift + right-click: pin an item to the top row (again: unpin).
scc.guide.tips.t.recent: Recently ordered: click fills in the order window, Shift + click orders again at once, right-click removes.
scc.guide.tips.t.rows: Crafting Terminal from 16 columns wide: the crafting grid moves next to your inventory - room for more rows.
scc.guide.tips.t.ru: R / U over an item: its recipes / uses in JEI or EMI - also for items that are only craftable.
scc.guide.tips.t.take: Click: a stack. Right-click: half. Ctrl + right-click: one. Shift + click: into your inventory.
scc.guide.tips.t.window: Drag a window by its title bar to keep it there; drag the corner grip to resize (terminal: Ctrl + grip sets the GUI scale).
scc.guide.tips.w.air: Middle-click into the air: the stack in your main hand goes into the network.
scc.guide.tips.w.default: Wireless Transmitter: Sneak + right-click with a receiver makes it your default - unlinked receivers you place connect to it.
scc.guide.tips.w.feed: Auto-feed (radio menu or Keep in inventory window): eats from the network when hungry - best saturation, no waste, nothing harmful unless allowed in the food row.
scc.guide.tips.w.pick: Pick Block (middle-click) on a block you don't carry: it comes from storage into your hand - or the order window opens. Switches in the radio menu of the terminal window.
scc.guide.tips.w.settings: Shift + right-click the wireless terminal: Keep in inventory, magnet, Repair with XP, FTB Quests.
scc.guide.tips.w.tools: Pick Block keeps tools in your hand: the block goes into a free hotbar slot (switch in the radio menu).
scc.guide.title: SCC Manual
scc.guide.tools.airstore: Store from the hand: with a linked wireless terminal on you (inventory or Curios) and within antenna range, middle-click into the air - no block or mob in the crosshair - and the stack in your main hand goes into the network. Only what fits; the rest stays in your hand. In creative mode only while sneaking. The terminal that makes the connection never goes in itself, and you need the "put" right. Turn it off in F7 (Terminal) if another mod uses that click.
scc.guide.tools.brush: Gives single blocks their own design. Right-click the air to pick one of the 27 designs (with a preview), then right-click any SCC block to paint it - machines, cables, frames, everything. Shift + right-click a block copies its design into the brush. Standard resets a block to the design each player picked under F7. A painted block looks the same for every player on the server. Breaking a block removes its paint. All 27 designs are loaded when the game starts, so painting never brings up a loading screen. If you turn off "Preload all designs" under F7, only the designs used in your world are loaded; a new one then shows after the next resource reload (F3+T).
scc.guide.tools.brush_gear: Since 1.4.0 the brush also paints Stellar Gear: gear in the off hand, brush in the main hand, right-click the air.
scc.guide.tools.card: Copies the settings of one SCC block onto another of the same kind. A Transfer Calculator with eighteen filter entries, a mode, a redstone rule and a priority is a quarter of an hour of clicking, and four of them used to be four of those. It copies between tiers of the same family too, so Red Dwarf to Blue Giant is fine. Contents are never copied - only what you set.
scc.guide.tools.dim: Removes the range limit entirely and lets the connection cross dimensions - in an Interface, Source then reaches Ars blocks in every dimension. Crafted around an Infinite Range Upgrade. One per block.
scc.guide.tools.effortless: Effortless Building: with a linked wireless terminal on you and within range, its build modes take the missing blocks out of the network (see Integrations).
scc.guide.tools.facade: A shell for a cable - or for any device sitting on one. Craft four iron nuggets around any full block, vanilla or modded, and you get four facades that look like it. Leave the middle empty and you get four blank facades instead: carry those and stamp one later by crafting it together with any block, one block per facade. The blank way costs more, the crossed way makes you decide before you leave. Put a facade on with right-click and the cable disappears into the wall: the block keeps a full block's shape, blocks light like a wall, and neighbouring blocks connect to it. A panel on that cable still looks out, with a rim of facade around it. Hold the wrench and every facade turns to a wireframe, so you can see the cabling you are about to work on.
scc.guide.tools.infinite: Removes the range limit within the dimension the antenna, transmitter or Interface stands in. Other dimensions need the Dimensional Upgrade. Crafted from eight Range Upgrades. One per block.
scc.guide.tools.logbook: The Star Logbook writes down your milestones in SCC with the in-game day - first network, first order, the first matter of each star tier, first star forging, first singularity, a caught meteor, Stellar Gear of every tier and more, about thirty in all. Right-click to open it: reached entries show their day, open ones stay grey with a short hint. A small notice pops up whenever a new one comes in.
scc.guide.tools.logbook2: The logbook keeps itself, with or without the book - the book is only the window. Each player has their own. What you had reached before the logbook existed is filled in from your advancements and marked "before the logbook".
scc.guide.tools.logbook3: The second tab, Statistics, counts for you: items you stored, finished orders and what they made, blocks your Star Quarries mined (also while you were away), wormhole jumps, meteors caught near you, meteor shower nights and Star Forge runs you watched. The numbers are kept on the server and fetched when you open the tab.
scc.guide.tools.magnet: Magnet: in the same window (Shift + right-click the wireless terminal, or Keep in inventory in the radio menu of the wireless terminal window), items you pick up go straight into the network - filtered by a whitelist or blacklist row. Magnet in the same menu, or a key you bind in the controls, switches it on and off without opening anything - also with the terminal in a Curios slot. Only within antenna range, and never what you just dropped yourself.
scc.guide.tools.nettool: Right-click any block of the network and it tells you what it is hanging on: which controller, how many devices, how much storage, how much power. It answers the question 'are these two cables actually the same network' without walking to a terminal.
scc.guide.tools.quests: FTB Quests only ever looks at your inventory, so a quest for 10,000 iron ignores the 10,000 sitting in your drives. Shift + right-click a wireless terminal and turn on Report to FTB Quests and the network counts too. It is off by default on purpose: it lets quests finish without the item ever passing through your hands, and that is your call, not ours. Nothing is taken from the network - only counted - and the antenna has to be in range, same as always.
scc.guide.tools.range: Adds 32 blocks of range to an antenna, a wireless transmitter or a Stellar Distributor. Up to eight fit into one block.
scc.guide.tools.remotectl: Controller from afar: the Controller entry in the radio menu of the wireless terminal window opens the Calculator Controller of the linked network - power and buffer, the Blocks list, the map and the rules, updated every second. View only: upgrading, load shedding and rules stay at the controller itself. Only within antenna range and with the "take" right; Esc brings you back to the terminal.
scc.guide.tools.wct: The same, with the crafting grid.
scc.guide.tools.wrench: Right-click turns a block without taking it apart - a Processing Calculator that ended up facing the wrong way keeps its filters. Shift + right-click takes one of our blocks down straight into your inventory, contents and settings included. On a cable with a facade the first shift-click takes only the facade, the second the cable. On the plate of a wall panel it takes only the device and leaves the cable that panel moved into - hit the core or an arm instead and the whole block comes up. On a Storage, Calculator or Crafting Monitor right-click switches the item between flat (2D) and block (3D).
scc.guide.tools.wt: The terminal in your pocket. Right-click a Network Antenna once to link it, and after that it opens anywhere in range.
scc.guide.tools.xprepair: Liquid experience in the network? Shift + right-click a wireless terminal and turn on Repair with XP: gear with Mending you carry is repaired from it, once a second, just like picking up XP orbs.
scc.help.cmd.balance: Shows the balance values that apply right now.
scc.help.cmd.balance.more: Lists the values pack makers can change with data packs (data/scc/scc_balance/...). Use it to check whether your data pack took effect.
scc.help.cmd.conjunction: Jumps to the peak of the next sky conjunction.
scc.help.cmd.conjunction.more: Sets the time in every world to the closest moment of the next conjunction, like /time set. Meant for testing and for showing the effect.
scc.help.cmd.doctor: Network report: machines and recipe types of the nearest network.
scc.help.cmd.doctor.more: Stand next to your network. Opens a report of what is connected, which recipe types the machines can run and where one is missing - the first thing to look at when an item seems impossible to craft. The report is also written to logs/scc.log.
scc.help.cmd.drain: Removes water from SCC blocks around you.
scc.help.cmd.drain.more: Repairs SCC blocks that an old bug left flooded: every waterlogged SCC block in the loaded chunks around you is drained (radius in chunks, default 8, 1-32). Cables you placed under water on purpose are drained as well.
scc.help.cmd.guide: Opens the SCC Manual, optionally at a chapter.
scc.help.cmd.guide.more: Opens the in-game manual, just like the SCC Manual item. With a chapter (for example start, network, storage, autocraft, processing, sky, forge, quarry, cosmos, power) it opens there; a second word jumps to a heading inside that chapter. Links in the chat use this command to point at the right page.
scc.help.cmd.help: Lists the SCC commands you may use, or explains one.
scc.help.cmd.help.more: Without an argument it lists every command you may use; click one to put it in the chat line. With a command name it shows the syntax, a description, an example and who may use it. Operators also get /scc help settings: every server setting with its current value, default and meaning.
scc.help.cmd.list: Shows all server settings with their values in a window.
scc.help.cmd.list.more: Opens a window with every setting, its value and a short explanation, with a search line. On the server console the list goes to the chat instead.
scc.help.cmd.meteor.more: Without a position it falls 24 to 48 blocks around you; with x y z it falls there. A Sky Harvester nearby catches it, otherwise it leaves a crater with a Meteorite - or burns up where blocks are protected. From the server console a position is required.
scc.help.cmd.order: Orders an item from your network by chat.
scc.help.cmd.order.more: Needs a linked Wireless Terminal in your inventory or Curios slot, in range of its antenna, and the right "order" on that network. Plans like the order window: if ingredients are missing, the chat lists them; otherwise the order starts and the chat shows the estimated time. Tab completes item IDs, items in your network first. Amount 1 to 1,000,000, default 1.
scc.help.cmd.power: Turns the power requirement of all networks on or off.
scc.help.cmd.power.more: Without on/off it shows the current value. Off: networks, machines and the Calculator Controller work without FE. Default: on.
scc.help.cmd.profile: Measures how much time SCC uses per tick.
scc.help.cmd.profile.more: /scc profile on starts measuring; play normally for a few minutes, then /scc profile shows the results in a window (and in logs/scc.log). /scc profile off stops it, /scc profile reset clears the measurements. Off by default and free while off.
scc.help.cmd.reloadconfig.more: Use it after editing the file by hand. The new values are sent to every player at once.
scc.help.cmd.rights: Shows the owner of the network and who has which rights.
scc.help.cmd.rights.more: Stand next to your network. Only the owner (or an operator) may see the list.
scc.help.cmd.selftest: Runs the SCC self-test at your position.
scc.help.cmd.selftest.more: Builds a small test network next to you, checks the basic functions and removes it again. Only failures and the total appear in the chat; the full run is in logs/scc.log - handy for bug reports. Use it where there is some free space.
scc.help.cmd.settings: Shows or changes a server setting.
scc.help.cmd.settings.more: /scc <setting> shows the current value, /scc <setting> <value> changes it at once for everyone and saves it in config/scc-server.json. On/off settings take on or off, all others a number in their allowed range. /scc help settings lists every setting with its default and meaning.
scc.help.cmd.shower: Tells when the next meteor shower night comes.
scc.help.cmd.shower.more: Shows whether a meteor shower is running right now or how long it is until the next one. Meteor showers come on new moon nights (settings meteorShowers, meteorShowerEvery, meteorShowerMeteors): shooting stars all night and a few real meteors per player.
scc.help.cmd.showerjump: Jumps to the sunset before the next meteor shower.
scc.help.cmd.showerjump.more: Sets the time in every world to just before sunset of the next meteor shower night, like /time set. Meant for testing and for showing the shower.
scc.help.cmd.sky: Shows the current and the next sky conjunction.
scc.help.cmd.sky.more: Tells you which sky conjunction is active right now, how long it still lasts and when the next one starts. During a conjunction the Sky Harvester gets double yield of the two sky objects involved (setting conjunctions).
scc.help.cmd.trust: Gives a player rights on your network.
scc.help.cmd.trust.more: Stand next to your network (within 12 blocks of an SCC block). Rights are take, put, order and build, separated by commas; without rights the player gets all of them. Only matters while the setting security is on. The Security Terminal does the same in a window.
scc.help.cmd.unstick: Frees all machines of the nearest network from stuck step filters.
scc.help.cmd.unstick.more: If orders keep reporting no matching machine although one is there, a step filter may be stuck. This command clears all of them; whatever is still inside the machines goes back to storage. Running jobs at most repeat one started step.
scc.help.cmd.untrust: Takes all rights on your network away from a player.
scc.help.cmd.untrust.more: Stand next to your network. While security is on, the player can no longer use it.
