scc.help.setting.calcEnergyPerTick: Calculators and devices (%s): FE per tick a device moves (0 = unlimited, -1 = use the datapack).
scc.help.setting.calcParallelJobs: Calculators (%s): jobs at the same time, 1-4096 (-1 = use the datapack).
scc.help.setting.calcRangeBonus: Network devices (%s): range in blocks a device adds to the network (-1 = use the datapack).
scc.help.setting.calcTicksPerOperation: Calculators and devices (%s): ticks per work step, 1-72000 (-1 = use the datapack scc_balance/tier).
scc.help.setting.chrononCost2x: Chronon per second for Time Dilation 2x (0 = free).
scc.help.setting.chrononCost4x: Chronon per second for Time Dilation 4x (0 = free).
scc.help.setting.chrononCost8x: Chronon per second for Time Dilation 8x (0 = free).
scc.help.setting.conjunctions: Do sky conjunctions give the Sky Harvester double yield of the two objects?
scc.help.setting.controllerCapacity: How much FE the controller holds.
scc.help.setting.controllerTransfer: How much FE may flow in per tick.
scc.help.setting.cradleBlast: Stellar Cradle: does a failed supernova explode and break blocks?
scc.help.setting.cradleFoodPerChronon: Stellar Cradle: how many eaten food items make one Chronon in a black hole (0 = none).
scc.help.setting.cradleRange: Stellar Cradle: range of gravitational interference and black hole mergers, in blocks.
scc.help.setting.cradleSpeed: Stellar Cradle: how fast star lifetimes run, in percent (100 = normal).
scc.help.setting.dilationStep: Time Dilation step %1$s: how many times faster the machine runs (default %2$sx; its cost is chrononCost%2$sx).
scc.help.setting.distBaseCost: Stellar Distributor base cost in 1/100 FE per tick (400 = 4 FE/t).
scc.help.setting.distDimensionalLoss: Stellar Distributor: loss in percent into another dimension (Dimensional).
scc.help.setting.distInfiniteLoss: Stellar Distributor: loss in percent beyond every range tier (Infinite Range).
scc.help.setting.distLossFree: Stellar Distributor: no transfer loss up to this many blocks.
scc.help.setting.distLossMax: Stellar Distributor: most loss by distance in percent.
scc.help.setting.distLossStep: Stellar Distributor: +1 % loss per this many blocks beyond that.
scc.help.setting.distRate: Stellar Distributor (%s): FE per tick for power and charging together.
scc.help.setting.distRate.unlimited: Stellar Distributor (%s): FE per tick for power and charging together (0 = unlimited).
scc.help.setting.distTargetCost: Stellar Distributor cost per supplied block in 1/100 FE per tick (10 = 0.1 FE/t).
scc.help.setting.distTargets: Stellar Distributor (%s): most blocks it supplies (1-1024).
scc.help.setting.factoryLog: Stellar Observatory: do networks record how busy their machines are (a few machines per second, kept for 30 days)?
scc.help.setting.forgeEnergy: Star Forge power cost in percent (100 = normal, 0 = free).
scc.help.setting.furnaceXp: Does a Processing Calculator send a furnace's experience into the network as liquid experience?
scc.help.setting.harvestEnergy: Sky Harvester power cost in percent (100 = normal, 0 = free).
scc.help.setting.harvestSpeed: Sky Harvester speed in percent (100 = normal).
scc.help.setting.instantCrafts: Single-step crafts a Singularity crafter finishes in the tick they arrive.
scc.help.setting.littleStarLightBlocks: Does the Little Star place invisible light blocks in dark places (as up to 1.4.0)? Off = it only glows on the client.
scc.help.setting.meteorChance: Chance per player and night that a meteor falls nearby, in percent.
scc.help.setting.meteorShowerEvery: Meteor showers: every how many new moon nights one comes (1 = every new moon, every 8 days).
scc.help.setting.meteorShowerMeteors: Meteor showers: real meteors per player in a shower night (0 = only shooting stars in the sky).
scc.help.setting.meteorShowers: Is every new moon night (see meteorShowerEvery) an announced meteor shower?
scc.help.setting.meteors: Do meteors fall at night (craters, or caught by a Sky Harvester)?
scc.help.setting.meteorsAvoidClaims: Do meteors avoid claimed chunks (FTB Chunks, Open Parties and Claims) and protected areas?
scc.help.setting.orbitMagicResistCap: Magic Ward satellite: highest magic damage reduction in percent.
scc.help.setting.orbitMagicResistPerStre: Magic Ward satellite: percent less magic damage per strength (one satellite = 1).
scc.help.setting.orderTimeout: Autocrafting: seconds a waiting order may stand still before it gives up, when neither the Calculator Controller nor the player (F7) chose a time (0 = built-in: 1 min, 6 min while a machine still works).
scc.help.setting.orderTimeoutMax: Autocrafting: the longest wait Calculator Controllers, players (F7) and Processing Calculators may choose, in seconds (0 = no limit, Never allowed).
scc.help.setting.overdrive: Does the Singularity Breaking Calculator have the Chronon Overdrive?
scc.help.setting.overdriveCost: Chronon Overdrive: Chronon per second on step %1$s (0 = free).
scc.help.setting.overdriveMax: Chronon Overdrive: blocks per second at the top step.
scc.help.setting.overdriveRampSeconds: Chronon Overdrive: seconds per step while speeding up (4 steps).
scc.help.setting.parallelSteps: Independent steps of one order that run at the same time as their own orders (0 = one step after another).
scc.help.setting.photonOutput: Sky Harvester photon mode output in percent (100 = normal, 0 = photon mode off).
scc.help.setting.photonRange: Blocks within which Sky Harvesters in photon mode share the sky (0 = no sharing).
scc.help.setting.powerFactor: All power costs in percent (100 = normal, 0 = free).
scc.help.setting.quarryFe: Star Quarry (%s): FE per block before hardness and cards.
scc.help.setting.quarryLoadsOwnChunk: Star Quarry: while it runs, does it keep its own chunk loaded and ticking (so it keeps mining with nobody nearby)? Released a few seconds after it stops, finishes or gets a redstone signal.
scc.help.setting.quarryLoadsWorkChunk: Star Quarry: does it keep the chunk it is mining loaded (max. 2 chunks, never its own)? Off: it only mines loaded chunks and comes back to the others later.
scc.help.setting.quarrySurveyBonus: Star Quarry: with a Quarry Survey Tool in its survey slot the area may be this many percent of the tier's side length (150 = 1.5x, 100 = no bonus).
scc.help.setting.quarryTicks: Star Quarry (%s): ticks per operation (lower = faster).
scc.help.setting.requireController: Does every network need a Calculator Controller?
scc.help.setting.security: Do players need rights on a network that is not theirs?
scc.help.setting.skyHarvesterNoSky: Can the Sky Harvester harvest matter without open sky (worlds without a sky, e.g. StoneBlock)? It then uses more power (skyHarvesterNoSkyCost). Photon mode still needs the sky.
scc.help.setting.skyHarvesterNoSkyCost: Sky Harvester power cost without sky, in percent of its normal cost (200 = double).
scc.help.setting.stockHistory: Terminal tooltips: record a 24-hour stock history per item (only items that change or are looked at)?
scc.help.setting.stockTooltips: Item tooltips: show players with a linked Wireless Terminal how many of the item their network holds?
scc.help.setting.storageChemicalPerTank: Chemical Storage (%s): mB per tank (0 = unlimited). A fuller storage keeps its contents and only refuses new inserts.
scc.help.setting.storageEnergy: Energy Storage (%s): FE it holds (0 = unlimited). A fuller storage keeps its contents and only refuses new inserts.
scc.help.setting.storageFluidPerTank: Fluid Storage (%s): mB per tank (0 = unlimited, at most 2,000,000,000). A fuller storage keeps its contents and only refuses new inserts.
scc.help.setting.storageItems: Item Storage (%s): items it holds, counted in items, not slots (0 = unlimited). A fuller storage keeps its contents and only refuses new inserts.
scc.help.setting.storageSouls: Soul Storage (%s): souls it holds (0 = unlimited). A fuller storage keeps its contents and only refuses new inserts.
scc.help.setting.storageSource: Source Storage (%s): Source it holds (0 = unlimited). A fuller storage keeps its contents and only refuses new inserts.
scc.help.setting.storageTanks: Fluid and Chemical Storage (%s): number of tanks, i.e. different fluids or chemicals (0 = unlimited). Also the slots of the Item Storage's 'one slot per type' void mode.
scc.help.setting.storageWarnPercent: Storage warning: from how many percent full (50-100). It warns again after the storage drops 5 points below.
scc.help.setting.storageWarnings: Warn players with terminal access when a network's storage reaches storageWarnPercent and when it is full?
scc.help.setting.timeDilation: The highest Time Dilation a Singularity Processing Calculator may use (1 = off, 8 = up to 8x).
scc.help.setting.timeDilationEnabled: Is there Time Dilation at all (Singularity Processing Calculator)? Off: no button, no machine is sped up.
scc.help.setting.wormholeBase: Wormhole Gate: FE every jump costs, however short.
scc.help.setting.wormholeCap: Most items a Singularity Transfer Calculator moves per run.
scc.help.setting.wormholeCooldown: Wormhole Gate: seconds before a player may jump again.
scc.help.setting.wormholeDimension: Wormhole Gate: FE for a jump into another dimension (replaces base and distance).
scc.help.setting.wormholeLeashed: Wormhole Gate: do leashed animals travel along?
scc.help.setting.wormholePerBlock: Wormhole Gate: FE per block of distance within one dimension.
scc.help.setting.wormholePreview: Wormhole Gate/Remote: send players a live picture of the destination inside the portal?
scc.help.setting.wormholeRemoteCooldown: Wormhole Remote: seconds before a player may open the next pocket rift.
scc.help.setting.wormholeRemoteCost: Wormhole Remote: price in percent of the gate price for the same jump.
scc.help.setting.wormholeRemoteOpen: Wormhole Remote: seconds a pocket rift stays open.
scc.help.setting.wormholeRemoteShared: Wormhole Remote: may other players walk through someone else's pocket rift?

scc.jei.avaritia_tables: Automation with SCC: put a Processing Calculator in front of this table. Orders from the network then run here - SCC lays out the ingredients in the right cells and takes the finished item out. One set at a time; a recipe needs its own table tier, as by hand.
scc.jei.chronon: Chronon only comes from a black hole in the Stellar Cradle: while it eats, every 40 food items (a bucket of fluid counts as one item) become one Chronon - about 1 per second when it is fully fed. It goes into the network, or into the cradle's output slot if the network has no room. Singularity Processing Calculators use it for Time Dilation: 2x costs 1, 4x costs 4, 8x costs 16 Chronon per second (settings: cradleFoodPerChronon, chrononCost2x/4x/8x).
scc.jei.cradle_build: Stellar Cradle: the core in the middle, eight Star Forge Frames around it on the same level and four Confinement Coils on the corners, one block higher. Keep the two blocks above the core free - the star floats there. A cable at any frame or under the core connects it. Right-click any part of the formed cradle, put in a star seed from the Star Forge, and it ignites.
scc.jei.design_brush: Design Brush: right-click the air to choose one of the 27 designs, right-click an SCC block to paint it, Shift + right-click a block to copy its design. Standard resets a block to each player's own F7 design. Painted blocks look the same for every player; breaking a block removes the paint. With Stellar Gear in the off hand, right-click the air paints the gear.
scc.jei.distributor: Stellar Distributor: hands the network's power, Source and charge to everything around it - no cables. Put in modules: FE Module for machines, Source Module for Ars Nouveau blocks, Charging Module for players' gear. 16 blocks of range, more with Range Upgrades; Infinite Range and Dimensional work as on the antenna. Costs 4 FE/t plus 0.1 FE/t per block, with a small transfer loss over distance. Upgrade it in the Star Forge.
scc.jei.draconic_fusion:
Automation with SCC: put a Processing Calculator in front of the Fusion Crafting Core. Orders from the network then run here - SCC puts the catalyst into the core and each ingredient into its own injector, starts the fusion and collects the result, one set at a time.

The injectors need power and the right tier, as by hand.
scc.jei.energizing_socket:
Energizing Socket - a compact base for Powah's Energizing Orb.

Place the orb on top and put real Energizing Rods into its 8 slots (right-click with a rod, or open it and shift-click). Each rod gives the orb exactly what it gives in the usual setup: same rate per tier, read from Powah's config, same 1-second warm-up. Without rods it charges nothing.

Power from an SCC cable or any FE cable straight into the socket; its buffer is as big as the rods' buffers together. A Processing Calculator facing the orb loads ingredients and takes out the result as usual.
scc.jei.facade: Two ways to a facade. Four iron nuggets around any full block, vanilla or modded, give four facades that look like that block. Four iron nuggets around an empty middle give four blank facades - craft a blank one together with any block and it takes that block's look, one for one. A blank facade can be stamped once; an already stamped one is not accepted, so a facade is never repainted with the old block lost. Put one on a cable with right-click and the cable vanishes into the wall - it keeps a full block's shape, blocks light like a wall, and neighbouring blocks connect to it. The network keeps running underneath. The wrench takes the facade off again with shift + right-click.
scc.jei.forge_build: Star Forge: the core in the middle, eight Star Forge Frames around it and one to four Focus Pylons on the corner frames. Keep the block above the core free. Once complete it forms into one machine - right-click any part. Hold a frame or pylon near the core to see which parts are missing. Put in the item one tier below plus the matter of the new tier (lenses from Yellow Star up: a lens prism). A cable at any frame or under the core connects it to the network - orders then use the forge directly.
scc.jei.gravity_gauntlet:
Gravity Gauntlet - lifts, holds and throws.

Right-click: lift a mob (up to 100 health), an item or a loose block (anything that falls like sand and gravel, and soft blocks like dirt and grass). It floats in front of you for up to 10 s. Right-click again: throw it.
Sneak + right-click: pull all items and XP within 10 blocks to you.

500 FE per lift, 5 FE per tick while holding, 1,000 FE per pull. Never players, bosses, other players' pets or blocks with an inventory; claims are respected. Charges like Stellar Gear (250k FE).
scc.jei.gravity_grenade:
Gravity Grenade - throw it like a snowball. Where it lands, a tiny violet black hole pulls every mob within 5 blocks to the middle for 3 seconds.

No damage, no block damage, no fall damage. Never pulls players, bosses or pets. In someone else's claim it fizzles.
scc.jei.gravity_lift: Gravity Lift: place two or more in one column (up to 64 blocks apart, free shaft) - they link with a soft beam of light. Stand on one and jump to ride up to the next, sneak to ride down. Smooth and fast, no fall damage in the beam. Each ride costs 50 FE + 5 FE per block - from its own buffer (any FE cable, Stellar Distributor with FE Module) or from an SCC network. Right-click with an empty hand shows its power.
scc.jei.harvester_build: Sky Harvester: the harvester at the bottom, two Harvester Masts on top, then insert a lens. It needs open sky and no rain. The lens decides how many sky objects it reaches; the matter goes into the network storage.
scc.jei.legacy_calculators: Old block from before 1.4.0. The Advanced and the Custom Processing Calculator are now modules of the Processing Calculator. Place it and it turns into a Processing Calculator of the same tier with its modules (Advanced: Routing + Supply, Custom: all three), keeping every setting and recipe - or craft it on its own (a Crafter works too) to get the Processing Calculator and the modules. Old ones in SCC storage convert on their own.
scc.jei.little_star:
Little Star - a tame companion that glows and collects.

Right-click a block: it appears and follows you, floating above your shoulder. It collects items within 6 blocks and hands them to you, never fights and cannot be hurt.

Right-click: sit / follow. Design Brush: paint it. Sneak + right-click with an empty hand: back into the item.
scc.jei.matter: Star matter. A Sky Harvester pulls it out of the sky - put a lens in it and build its tower (two Harvester Masts). The lens decides which of the five sky objects it reaches.
scc.jei.meteorite: Meteorites fall at night now and then (in worlds with the Overworld sky), 24 to 48 blocks from a player. A Sky Harvester in range catches them; otherwise they leave a small crater with a glowing Meteorite in the middle. Mine it for ores (vanilla and from other mods) and Star Shards. Never in claimed chunks or next to bases. Settings: /scc meteors, /scc meteorChance. OPs: /scc meteor.
scc.jei.mini_sun:
Mini Sun - a small floating sun.

Place it on a block, or right-click into the air to throw it: where it lands it floats up and stays.

Light 15 all around (invisible lights in a ring), no natural monster spawns within 16 blocks, plants within 8 blocks grow about 50% faster.

10 FE/t while lit, own 250k FE buffer. Refills from an SCC cable, other mods' cables (1,000 FE/t) or as an item at the Stellar Distributor. Right-click: on/off.
scc.jei.modules: Modules for the Stellar Distributor. FE Module: powers every machine in range (batteries and SCC blocks are left out unless you allow batteries). Source Module: every Ars Nouveau block in range draws the network's Source. Charging Module: charges the gear of permitted players in range, no wireless terminal needed.
scc.jei.observatory: Stellar Observatory: factory analysis for its network. Every network with a controller records in the background how its machines spend their time (working, waiting, blocked, idle) and why, the power they use and how long orders take. The observatory shows bottlenecks with percentages, suggestions with an estimated gain, curves for the last hour, day and month, and a map of where it jams. A hologram above the block shows the most important numbers.
scc.jei.orbit_satellites:
Orbit Satellites - up to 4 small satellites orbit you (6 with an expanded pedestal).

Put an Orbit Formation in the middle of a Constellation Pedestal and the satellites in the ring. The formation then works anywhere in your inventory (or a Curios charm slot); right-click it to switch it on and off. Constellation Expansion I and II unlock slots 5 and 6 on the pedestal.

Collector: pulls items and XP (6 to 16 blocks), into storage when linked.
Gunner: star bolts at hostile mobs (2 hearts, +50% against undead).
Healer: half a heart every 3 s, cleanses and absorbs when stronger.
Lantern: light, enemies glow and take 15% more damage, no monster spawns.
Shield: catches a projectile every 8 s.
Repair: slowly repairs worn and held gear.
Comet: speed and step assist.
Magic Ward: less magic damage (only with a magic mod).

Same role next to each other: +35% each. All roles different (4 or more): +20%. Combos: Gunner + Lantern, Healer + Shield. Power: the formation's own 250k FE, then a worn Stellar Exo chestplate.
scc.jei.photons: Photon mode: switch a Sky Harvester from Matter to Photons in its window and it feeds starlight into the network as power, using none itself - enough to start an empty network. Per lens: Basic 50, Red Dwarf 120, Yellow Star 300, Blue Giant 600, Neutron Star 1,000, Singularity 1,600 FE/t, times the height of its objects. Rain stops it; photon harvesters within 16 blocks share the sky.
scc.jei.planetarium:
Planetarium - the control centre of your Stellar Gear.

Right-click: charge and tier of everything you carry, every effect with its switch, Orbit Formation on/off and your Little Stars (sit/follow, call).

Only the player who placed it can use it.
scc.jei.processor_modules: Modules for the Processing Calculator. Open its window and click an empty module slot on the right: the module comes from storage or your inventory, otherwise the order window opens (Ctrl+click orders right away) and the finished module goes in on its own. Shift+click takes a module out. Routing: side configuration for items, fluids and chemicals plus ports. Supply: fuel, liquid fuel and FE kept topped up. Custom Pattern: your own recipes. Without modules the calculator still detects the machine, feeds it and collects the results.
scc.jei.raven_infusion:
Automation with SCC: put a Processing Calculator in front of the Enchanting Table of the Raven. Orders for infusion recipes then run here - SCC sets Eterna, Quanta and Arcana to what each recipe needs, infuses the item and puts your own values back afterwards.

Each infusion costs 3 Lapis Lazuli and liquid experience from the network, as by hand.

A normal enchanting table works too: then the values of its bookshelves count, and the order tells you if they do not reach the recipe.
scc.jei.sky_sensor:
Sky Sensor - a redstone signal from the sky.

Right-click to choose: conjunction, star above X°, star at its peak, meteor approaching, meteor shower, night, day, new moon or the harvest factor of a star. Invert swaps on and off.

A comparator reads a graded value (height of the star, closeness of a conjunction, number of meteors). Needs no network, power or open sky.
scc.jei.soul_storage: Souls from Industrial Foregoing Souls are a resource of the SCC network. In: a Storage Connector or Transfer Calculator on top of a Soul Laser Base, or Soul Pipes into an SCC Interface set to Accept. Out: Soul Pipes and Soul Surges at an SCC Interface set to Supply (the default).
scc.jei.star_chart: Right-click for a map of the sky: which objects stand high now and next, the moon phase with countdowns, the next conjunction (double harvest for 10 minutes) and a photon forecast for any lens over the next Minecraft day.
scc.jei.star_forging.tip: The pylons charge the forge with this much power per item, then the workpiece rises one tier. Up to 64 go through in one reaction.
scc.jei.star_lasso:
Star Lasso - catches a mob in a Star Bubble.

Right-click a mob with an empty Star Bubble in your inventory. Passive and neutral mobs up to 100 health (cows, horses, villagers, iron golems): 1,000 FE. Hostile mobs up to 40 health, and only once they are at half health or less: 5,000 FE.
Right-click a block with a filled bubble to release the mob - name, health, gear and trades stay. The bubble is empty again.

Never players, bosses or other players' pets; claims are respected.
scc.jei.star_life: A star's life in the Stellar Cradle: Red Dwarf 80 FE/t for 24 hours - Yellow Star 500 FE/t for 10 hours (Sun Cores keep it burning) - Blue Giant 2,500 FE/t for 3 hours, then a supernova. If the coils charge a 2,000,000 FE barrier, 2 Neutronium and a Pulsar remain (10,000 FE/t in bursts, spun up with Neutronium). 4 Dark Matter collapse the Pulsar into a Black Hole that eats items and fluids from the network - up to 40,000 FE/t. Seeds: Protostar Shell plus star matter in the Star Forge.
scc.jei.star_logbook: Keeps your milestones in SCC with the in-game day: first network, first order, the first matter of every star tier, first Star Forge product, first singularity, first Chronon, a caught meteor, a finished quarry pit, Stellar Gear of every tier and more. Right-click to read it; entries you have not reached yet stay grey with a hint. Every player has their own logbook, and it keeps writing even without the book.
scc.jei.star_quarry: Mines a whole area layer by layer. Set the area in its window or stake it out with Quarry Markers; drops go into the network, a chest next to it or its own buffer. Power per block grows with the tier, and so does the speed: Basic 800 FE/block at 2 blocks/s (about 80 FE/t), Red Dwarf 1,000 (200 FE/t), Yellow Star 1,200 (600 FE/t), Blue Giant 1,500 (1,500 FE/t), Neutron Star 2,000 (4,000 FE/t), Singularity 2,500 at 120 blocks/s (about 15,000 FE/t) - more in hard rock and with cards. Card slots: one on Basic, one more per tier, six on Singularity. Field size: 32×32 on Basic, 64, 128, 256, 512 and 1000×1000 on Singularity; the top layer can lie up to the build limit above the core.
scc.jei.star_shield:
Star Shield - blocks like a shield, never breaks, flashes with every block.

Star Mirror: projectiles hitting the raised shield from the front fly back where you look (250 FE).

Tiers at the Star Anvil: Red Dwarf Ember Rim (attackers burn), Yellow Star Guide Beam (back to the shooter), Blue Giant Plasma Push, Neutron Star Dense Mirror (arrows x2), Singularity Nova Flash.

Charges like Stellar Gear.
scc.jei.starlight: Starlight: lamps, glass and path slabs in the five star colours, gently pulsing, light level 15. Lamps from glowstone and the star matter of the colour, glass from clear glass, paths from three lamps (or the stonecutter). Eight of one kind + a dye recolors them: red, yellow, light blue, white, purple.
scc.jei.stellar_blade:
Stellar Blade - a sword on FE, from 9 to 31 attack damage.

Red Dwarf: Red Harvest (Looting +1, heal on kill)
Yellow Star: Sun Flash (right-click)
Blue Giant: Plasma Arc (a full swing throws a sickle)
Neutron Star: Gravity Strike (full hit)
Singularity: Time Stop (hold right-click, costs a Chronon)

Star Anvil: Chronon Resonance (+1 damage each). Modules: Star Edge, Armor Breaker, Critical Strike, Looting.

Bosses are only slowed - never frozen, pulled or blinded.
scc.jei.stellar_bow:
Stellar Bow - a bow on FE.

With FE it fires plasma arrows (100 FE each, no arrows needed) and draws faster; without FE it is a normal bow with arrows from your inventory.

Red Dwarf: Ember Shot (burning arrows, Looting +1)
Yellow Star: Solar Volley (3 arrows in a fan)
Blue Giant: Plasma Bolt (straight, through 3 targets)
Neutron Star: Gravity Arrow (pulls enemies together)
Singularity: Seeking Star (arrows curve towards enemies)

The strong effects need a fully drawn bow. Bosses are only slowed.
scc.jei.stellar_drill:
Stellar Drill - pickaxe, axe and shovel in one. Runs on FE instead of durability: at 0 FE it never breaks, it just gets slow.

Red Dwarf: Ember (autosmelt)
Yellow Star: Hammer 3×3 + Sunpower
Blue Giant: 5×5 / depth 3, Silk/Fortune switch, Plasma Cutter
Neutron Star: Network Link (drops into storage)
Singularity: Black Hole Drill Head (whole veins and trees)

Sneak + right-click: settings. Charge it at a Stellar Distributor (full speed) or wirelessly with Charge gear (a quarter).
scc.jei.stellar_exo:
Stellar Exo - Netherite armor on FE instead of durability (each piece: its Netherite piece + 2 Stellar Steel). Every piece is upgraded on its own in the Star Anvil; an effect works when the piece that carries it has the tier.

Star Hull: each piece absorbs damage with FE - 15% to 75% per tier, a full Singularity set everything.

Leggings, Red Dwarf: Core Heat (no freezing, fire and lava a quarter)
Helmet, Yellow Star: Solar Skin (charges in sunlight)
Chestplate, Blue Giant: Plasma Shield (3 charges)
Boots, Neutron Star: Gravity Boots (walls, ceilings, no fall damage)
Chestplate, Singularity: Event Horizon (swallows projectiles)
All four on Singularity: Flight

At 0 FE the Netherite protection stays, only the hull and the effects stop.
scc.jei.stellar_gear:
Stellar Gear - your own tools from Netherite upwards.

Stellar Steel: Netherite Ingot + 4 Red Dwarf Ember in the Star Forge.
Star Cores: 2 Stellar Steel + 4 star matter of the tier in the Star Forge.
Star Anvil: tool + core of the next tier = tool one tier higher; enchantments stay. The anvil also switches effects on and off.
scc.jei.stellar_modules:
Stellar Modules - extras for the Stellar Exo, Drill, Blade and Bow, forged in the Star Forge.

Each module item is one level: install it in the module window (sneak + right-click the gear, then "Modules"). A piece has tier + 1 slots and a core load budget, so you have to choose. The highest level depends on the tier of the piece.

Looting and Fortune go up to the Apothic Enchanting maximum when it is installed, otherwise III.
scc.jei.stellar_pocket:
Stellar Pocket - a tool bag for your belt or charm slot (Curios) or simply your inventory.

Press G (rebindable under Controls): tap it to put the tool in your hand back into the pocket; hold it, point at a tool and let go to take it - the tool you held takes its place. Tap it while looking at a block and the pocket hands you its best tool for that block. With an empty hand a tap into the air keeps the wheel open: click a tool or press 1-9.

Tools, weapons, gadgets and Stellar Gear fit - SCC's own tools too, and those of other mods (anything with durability, tagged as a tool or battery-powered, and portable crafting stations like Crafting on a Stick). No blocks, armor, food or containers. 9 slots; at a Smithing Table with a Star Shard (template) and a Stellar Steel Ingot it grows to 18, then 27 - the tools stay inside.
scc.jei.stock.craftable: Missing, but the network can build it:
scc.jei.wormhole: Wormhole Gate: right-click it for a list of every gate on the same network, with dimension, distance and price. Click one and you arrive standing on top of it. A jump costs 1,000 FE plus 10 FE per block, 50,000 FE into another dimension - paid from the network above the controller's reserve. Gates in other dimensions join through a wireless bridge with a Dimensional Upgrade. Name a gate in its window or in an anvil.
scc.jei.wormhole_remote: Wormhole Remote: link it to a Network Antenna or Wormhole Gate (right-click), then right-click into the air for the list of gates on that network. Pick one and a rift opens in front of you for 10 seconds - walk in and you arrive on top of that gate, and others may follow. Costs the gate price plus 50% from the network. Range like a Wireless Terminal: other dimensions only with a Dimensional Upgrade in the antenna.
scc.jeisync.tip: Send the search text to JEI / EMI
scc.lasso.no.big: Too big for a Star Bubble
scc.lasso.no.bubble: You need an empty Star Bubble
scc.lasso.no.claim: Not here - this area is protected
scc.lasso.no.healthy: Weaken it first (half health or less)
scc.legacy.notice.guide.tip: Opens the SCC Manual at Processing > Modules
scc.legacy.notice.head: SCC 1.4.0:
scc.legacy.notice.many: Advanced and Custom Processing Calculators are now one Processing Calculator with modules (Routing, Supply, Custom Pattern). Your %s calculators were converted - nothing was lost.
scc.legacy.notice.one: Advanced and Custom Processing Calculators are now one Processing Calculator with modules (Routing, Supply, Custom Pattern). Your calculator was converted - nothing was lost.
scc.legacy.notice.toast: SCC 1.4.0: %s old calculators converted - see chat
scc.lens.objects: Reaches %s of the five sky objects:
scc.lift.blocked: Gravity Lift: no headroom above the target lift - keep 2 blocks free (no carpet or slab on top).
scc.lift.nopower: Gravity Lift: not enough power (%s FE) - charge it with an FE cable, a Stellar Distributor (FE Module) or connect it to an SCC network.
scc.lift.status.empty: Gravity Lift: no power (%s / %s FE) - it stands still. Charge it with an FE cable, a Stellar Distributor (FE Module) or an SCC network.
scc.lift.status.free: Gravity Lift: rides are free on this server (power is off).
scc.lift.status.net: Gravity Lift: %s / %s FE stored - the SCC network pays when it runs out.
scc.lift.tip.1: Stack two or more in one column. Jump: ride up. Sneak: ride down.
scc.lift.tip.2: Up to %s blocks apart, with a free shaft in between. No fall damage in the beam.
scc.lift.tip.3: Each ride costs %s FE + %s FE per block - from its own small buffer (any FE cable, or a Stellar Distributor with FE Module) or from an SCC network. No SCC network needed.
scc.logic.btn.export.tip: Copy a share code of the selection - or of the whole plan - to the clipboard (Ctrl+E)
scc.logic.btn.import.tip: Insert a share code from the clipboard next to your plan (Ctrl+I)
scc.logic.btn.library.tip: Save plans with a name and load them again - also in other worlds (Ctrl+L)
scc.logic.calc.noprocs: This network has no Processing Calculator yet. Place one in front of a machine and connect it to the network.
scc.logic.copied.nodes: %s node(s) copied - also as a share code in the clipboard
scc.logic.desc.blink: Switches on and off while its input is on - adjustable on and off time in ticks (20 ticks = 1 second).
scc.logic.desc.calc: Pauses one Processing Calculator of this network while the input is 0: nothing new goes in, results still come out.
scc.logic.desc.clock: Gives 1 once every N seconds, otherwise 0 - a heartbeat for counters and repeated actions.
scc.logic.desc.compare: 1 if A and B fulfil the comparison, otherwise 0.
scc.logic.desc.counter: Counts how often the input jumps from 0 to something else; Reset sets it back to 0.
scc.logic.desc.daytime: 1 during the day - or during the night, if switched.
scc.logic.desc.delay: Passes the input on only after it stayed the same for N seconds.
scc.logic.desc.display: Shows the input big in the node - for watching values live. Does nothing else.
scc.logic.desc.edge: 1 for one tick when the input jumps from 0 to something else.
scc.logic.desc.jobend: Gives 1 for one tick when an order of this network finishes (or fails). Optionally only for one item.
scc.logic.desc.jobs: Number of running and waiting jobs in the network.
scc.logic.desc.latch: Remembers: Set turns it on, Reset turns it off. Loops through it are allowed.
scc.logic.desc.machine: Watches one Processing Calculator of this network: is its machine idle, full, or how full in percent.
scc.logic.desc.math: A + B, A - B, A * B, A / B, minimum or maximum.
scc.logic.desc.message: Sends the text when the input switches on - to the owner or everyone with network access, in chat or above the hotbar.
scc.logic.desc.note: Just text - explain what your plan does. Notes are never evaluated.
scc.logic.desc.onorder: How many of the item running and waiting orders will still deliver.
scc.logic.desc.or: 1 if at least one input is not 0.
scc.logic.desc.order: Orders the item through the network planner. "Fill up" orders target - stock - on order; "On edge" orders a fixed amount when the input switches on. Never two open orders at once.
scc.logic.desc.player: Online: how many players are online, or 1 if the named player is. Nearby: players within range of this block.
scc.logic.desc.power: Fill level of the network power buffer in percent (0-100).
scc.logic.desc.radio_rx: Receives the value sent on a channel by another Logic Calculator of yours (or your team) - even in another network or dimension.
scc.logic.desc.radio_tx: Sends its input on a channel. Every Logic Calculator of yours (or your team) can receive it.
scc.logic.desc.redstone: The strongest redstone signal reaching this block, 0-15. Sides it powers itself are ignored.
scc.logic.desc.redstone_out: Emits redstone on one side or all sides - e.g. to a lamp or a Toggle Bus. The mode sets the strength.
scc.logic.desc.route: The exact path through your machines: raw material, then machine after machine (e.g. Raw Iron -> Enrichment Chamber -> Furnace). Connect it to the Route input of Order nodes; only their orders go this way.
scc.logic.desc.stock: How many of the item are in the network right now. Fluids count in mB.
scc.logic.desc.surplus: Moves everything above the kept amount into an inventory next to this block. Destroying is a separate setting.
scc.logic.desc.xor: 1 if exactly one input is not 0.
scc.logic.destroy.0.tip: Into the inventory on the chosen side. If it is full, nothing is removed.
scc.logic.destroy.1.tip: Deletes the surplus for good - only if you really mean it.
scc.logic.destroy.warn: Warning: everything above the kept amount is deleted for good. It cannot be brought back.
scc.logic.eg.blink: e.g. Order Busy -> Blinker -> Redstone out (alarm light)
scc.logic.eg.calc: e.g. Power < 20 % -> NOT -> Calculator on/off (pause a hungry machine)
scc.logic.eg.jobend: e.g. Job failed -> Message "Check the furnace!"
scc.logic.eg.latch: e.g. on below 20 % power, off above 50 %
scc.logic.eg.machine: e.g. Machine idle -> Redstone out (a lamp that says "done")
scc.logic.eg.order: e.g. Fill up Iron Ingot to 1000
scc.logic.eg.player: e.g. Player nearby -> AND -> Order (only while you are home)
scc.logic.eg.radio_rx: e.g. Radio "alarm" -> Redstone out in your base
scc.logic.eg.redstone_out: e.g. Compare -> Redstone out -> a lamp next to the block
scc.logic.eg.route: e.g. Iron Ingot <- Blast Furnace only
scc.logic.eg.surplus: e.g. keep 10,000 Cobblestone, the rest into a chest below
scc.logic.empty.body: A plan reads the network, decides and acts - left to right. The quickest start is a template: insert it, then click its nodes and adjust them.
scc.logic.empty.help: Or drag a node from the palette · F1: controls
scc.logic.empty.title: Your plan is empty
scc.logic.err.calcgone: The chosen Processing Calculator is not in this network (any more).
scc.logic.err.double: an input can only have one connection
scc.logic.err.internal: This node hit an error - see logs/scc.log.
scc.logic.err.jobfailed: Last order failed (%s) - waits before ordering again.
scc.logic.err.loop: The target belongs to this network - items would only go round in circles.
scc.logic.err.nofluid: Fluids cannot be removed this way.
scc.logic.err.noplanner: No player online to plan with.
scc.logic.err.notarget: No inventory on that side of the block.
scc.logic.err.noterminal: No terminal in the network - orders need one.
scc.logic.err.rejected: The terminal did not accept the order (queue full or plan outdated) - tries again.
scc.logic.err.rights: you lack the Build right on this network
scc.logic.err.rightstake: you lack the Take right on this network (needed for Remove surplus)
scc.logic.err.route: Recipe not runnable: no machine for %s in the network.
scc.logic.err.routelink: a recipe route only fits the Route input
scc.logic.export.empty: Nothing to export - the plan is empty.
scc.logic.export.plan: Share code of the whole plan copied (%s nodes, %s characters)
scc.logic.export.selection: Share code of the selection copied (%s nodes, %s characters)
scc.logic.fix.calcgone: Choose the calculator again - it was removed, moved or is cut off from the network.
scc.logic.fix.jobfailed: Open the terminal's job list to see why; the node waits longer after each failure.
scc.logic.fix.loop: Put a chest, trash can or another network's interface on that side instead.
scc.logic.fix.missing: Put the missing ingredients into the network - it tries again by itself.
scc.logic.fix.nocalc: Click the calculator field in the inspector and pick one from the list.
scc.logic.fix.nochannel: Type a channel name in the inspector - the same name on sender and receiver.
scc.logic.fix.nofluid: Choose an item - for fluids use a Rules entry of the controller.
scc.logic.fix.noinventory: Use Idle instead - this machine does not show its slots.
scc.logic.fix.noitem: Click the item field in the inspector and choose one.
scc.logic.fix.noplanner: Orders are planned on a player's game - it continues as soon as someone with access is online.
scc.logic.fix.norecipe: Check in the terminal whether the item can be crafted at all (recipe, machines).
scc.logic.fix.notarget: Place a chest (or any inventory) on the chosen side, or choose another side.
scc.logic.fix.noterminal: Place a Network Terminal anywhere in this network.
scc.logic.fix.rejected: Usually the terminal's queue is full - it tries again by itself.
scc.logic.fix.route: Connect that machine to the network with a Processing Calculator, or change the route.
scc.logic.fix.targetfull: Empty the target or use a bigger one - nothing is lost meanwhile.
scc.logic.help.auto.off: Open the inspector when I select a node: off
scc.logic.help.auto.on: Open the inspector when I select a node: on
scc.logic.help.auto.tip: With the inspector hidden, selecting a node opens it - and it hides again when you deselect.
scc.logic.help.c1: Drag a node from the palette onto the board - or click it to place it in the middle.
scc.logic.help.c10: There is no save button: every change is saved a moment later.
scc.logic.help.c2: Drag from an output dot (right) to an input dot (left) to connect.
scc.logic.help.c3: Drag a connected input away to remove the connection.
scc.logic.help.c4: Mouse wheel zooms at the cursor, dragging the empty board pans, F fits everything.
scc.logic.help.c5: Shift+drag selects several nodes; Del deletes; Ctrl+A selects all.
scc.logic.help.c6: Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y undo and redo; Ctrl+C / Ctrl+V copy nodes - also between worlds.
scc.logic.help.c7: Tab hides or shows both side panels; the arrows hide one of them.
scc.logic.help.c8: T templates · Ctrl+L library · Ctrl+E export · Ctrl+I import.
scc.logic.help.c9: Hover anything - palette entries, fields, dots - for an explanation.
scc.logic.help.lit: A connection lights up and carries pulses of light while its value is not 0.
scc.logic.help.title: Logic Calculator - controls and legend
scc.logic.help.values: Every node shows its live value in its title bar. A red node has a problem - hover it to see what to do.
scc.logic.hint: Wheel: zoom · Drag: pan · Shift+drag: select · Del · Ctrl+Z/Y/C/V · Tab: panels · F1: help
scc.logic.import.damaged: The share code is damaged or cut off - copy it again completely.
scc.logic.import.empty: The clipboard is empty - copy a share code (SCC-LOGIC:...) first.
scc.logic.import.full: No room: the code has %s nodes, only %s more fit (at most 96).
scc.logic.import.mods: %s node(s) imported; %s item(s) from missing mods (%s) shown in red
scc.logic.import.notcode: The clipboard holds no plan - a share code starts with SCC-LOGIC:
scc.logic.import.ok: Imported %s node(s) next to your plan
scc.logic.import.types: This plan uses nodes this SCC version does not know (%s) - update SCC.
scc.logic.inspector.many: %s nodes selected - drag to move them, Del deletes, Ctrl+C copies.
scc.logic.inspector.none: Select a node to edit it.
scc.logic.inspector.step1: Sources (cyan) read the network: stock, power, machines, players.
scc.logic.inspector.step2: Logic (violet) compares and combines - e.g. stock < 1000.
scc.logic.inspector.step3: Actions (gold) do something: order, redstone, message, pause a calculator.
scc.logic.inspector.step4: Drag from an output dot to an input dot. Square dots are on/off, round dots are numbers.
scc.logic.io.delay: In: value · Out: the value, N seconds later
scc.logic.io.message: In: On (sends when it switches on)
scc.logic.io.order: In: On, Target, Route · Out: Busy
scc.logic.io.radio_rx: Out: received number (0 if nobody sends)
scc.logic.io.route: Out: Route - only into the Route input of Order
scc.logic.jobend.any.tip: Fires when an order ends, done or failed.
scc.logic.jobend.done.tip: Fires when an order is completed.
scc.logic.jobend.failed.tip: Fires when an order gives up (missing items, no machine ...). Orders cancelled by a player do not count.
scc.logic.lib.empty: No saved plans yet. Give your plan a name above and save it - it ends up as a text file you can back up and share.
scc.logic.lib.err.noname: Give the plan a name first.
scc.logic.lib.err.write: Could not write the file - is the folder read-only?
scc.logic.lib.folder.tip: Opens %s - back up plans or drop in files from friends
scc.logic.lib.insert.tip: Add it next to your plan (double-click works too)
scc.logic.lib.intro: Plans you save here are files in your game folder - they stay when you change worlds or servers.
scc.logic.lib.load.tip: Replace the current plan with this one (Ctrl+Z brings yours back)
scc.logic.lib.loaded: Loaded "%s" - Ctrl+Z brings your old plan back
scc.logic.lib.name: Name...
scc.logic.lib.noname: Give the plan a name first.
scc.logic.lib.save.tip: Saves as a readable text file - a plan with the same name is replaced
scc.logic.lib.title: Plan library
scc.logic.mode.edge.tip: Orders a fixed amount each time the On input switches on.
scc.logic.mode.fill.tip: Keeps the item at the target: orders what is missing.
scc.logic.note.empty: Empty note - type your text in the inspector.
scc.logic.op.div: A divided by B (whole numbers; B = 0 gives 0)
scc.logic.op.ge: A greater than or equal to B
scc.logic.op.le: A less than or equal to B
scc.logic.op.max: The larger of A and B
scc.logic.op.min: The smaller of A and B
scc.logic.param.name: Player name
scc.logic.player.near.tip: Players within the range of this block, in this dimension.
scc.logic.portdesc.calc.out: 1 while the calculator runs, 0 while it is paused.
scc.logic.portdesc.latch.reset: On switches the latch off again.
scc.logic.portdesc.latch.set: On switches the latch on - it stays on.
scc.logic.portdesc.order.busy: 1 while an order of this node is being planned or running.
scc.logic.portdesc.order.route: Connect a Recipe route: its recipes are forced for this node's orders.
scc.logic.portdesc.order.target: The target stock as a number - overrides the Target field.
scc.logic.portdesc.surplus.out: How many items were moved in the last half second.
scc.logic.porttip.drag.in: Drop a connection here; drag it away to remove it.
scc.logic.porttip.drag.out: Drag from here to an input.
scc.logic.porttip.fixed: not connected - uses the value set in the inspector
scc.logic.ptip.a: Value used for A while nothing is connected to A.
scc.logic.ptip.amount: How many to order each time the input switches on.
scc.logic.ptip.b: Value used for B while nothing is connected to B - e.g. the limit of a comparison.
scc.logic.ptip.batch: Round every order up to a multiple of this (0 = exactly the gap). Bigger batches mean fewer machine runs.
scc.logic.ptip.blink.on: 1 = blink, 0 = off. Unconnected it blinks all the time.
scc.logic.ptip.calc.on: 1 = the calculator runs, 0 = paused. A pause ends by itself about a second after this block stops sending it.
scc.logic.ptip.calc.pos: The Processing Calculator to pause. Only calculators of this network can be chosen.
scc.logic.ptip.channel: Channel name. Senders and receivers with the same name are connected - only between your own (or your team's) Logic Calculators.
scc.logic.ptip.cooldown: Minimum seconds between two actions of this node.
scc.logic.ptip.delay.secs: The input must stay the same this long before the output follows.
scc.logic.ptip.destroy: Move into the inventory next to the block, or destroy. Destroying cannot be undone.
scc.logic.ptip.high: How long the output stays on, in ticks (20 = 1 second). 0 = never on.
scc.logic.ptip.in: Value used while the input is not connected.
scc.logic.ptip.item: The item this node works with. Click to choose, right-click to clear.
scc.logic.ptip.jobend.item: Empty = any order of this network. Otherwise only orders of this item.
scc.logic.ptip.keep: This many stay in the network; only what is above gets removed.
scc.logic.ptip.low: How long the output stays off, in ticks. 0 = always on while the input is on.
scc.logic.ptip.machine.pos: The Processing Calculator whose machine is watched. Only calculators of this network can be chosen.
scc.logic.ptip.message.cooldown: Minimum seconds between two messages - so an alarm does not flood the chat.
scc.logic.ptip.message.on: The message is sent when this switches from 0 to on.
scc.logic.ptip.mode: How this node works - hover a button for details.
scc.logic.ptip.name: Empty = any player. Otherwise exactly this player name.
scc.logic.ptip.night: Day: 1 during the day. Night: 1 during the night.
scc.logic.ptip.note: What you want to explain. Long text wraps inside the note.
scc.logic.ptip.on: 1 = on, 0 = off - used while the On input is not connected.
scc.logic.ptip.onorder.item: The item whose open orders are counted.
scc.logic.ptip.op: The operation - hover a button to see what it does.
scc.logic.ptip.order.cooldown: Minimum seconds between two orders of this node - also after a failed attempt.
scc.logic.ptip.order.item: The item to order. It is planned with the whole recipe tree, like in the terminal.
scc.logic.ptip.order.mode: Fill up: keeps the item at the target. On edge: orders a fixed amount each time On switches on.
scc.logic.ptip.order.on: 1 = this order may run. Usually connected to a Compare.
scc.logic.ptip.pos: Which Processing Calculator of this network. Click to choose from the list, right-click to clear.
scc.logic.ptip.range: How far from this block a player may be, at most 64 blocks.
scc.logic.ptip.rate: At most this many items per half second (1-1024) - keeps the server smooth.
scc.logic.ptip.redstone_out.mode: On/off: any value except 0 gives full strength 15. Strength: the value itself, 0-15.
scc.logic.ptip.redstone_out.side: Which side gives the signal - or all sides. A lamp or Toggle Bus right next to the block reacts directly.
scc.logic.ptip.reset: 1 switches it off (or back to 0) - Reset wins over Set.
scc.logic.ptip.set: 1 switches the latch on - while the Set input is not connected.
scc.logic.ptip.side: Which side of the block. Sides are world directions (north, east ...), not where the block faces.
scc.logic.ptip.style: Chat line or a short text above the hotbar.
scc.logic.ptip.surplus.item: The item whose surplus is removed. Fluids are not supported.
scc.logic.ptip.surplus.on: 1 = remove surplus now, 0 = wait. Unconnected it always works.
scc.logic.ptip.surplus.side: The side where the target inventory (chest, trash can, another network's interface) touches this block.
scc.logic.ptip.target: Stock to reach: orders target - stock - on order. Connect the Target input to make it variable.
scc.logic.ptip.to: Owner = only who placed the block. Everyone = all players with access to this network.
scc.logic.ptip.w: Width of the note on the board (96-360).
scc.logic.ptip.what: What this node reacts to - hover a button for details.
scc.logic.rail.inspector.hide: Hide the inspector (Tab hides both sides)
scc.logic.rail.palette.hide: Hide the palette (Tab hides both sides)
scc.logic.route.add.none: No known recipe uses %s. Add an own step and tell SCC what the machine makes.
scc.logic.route.add.title: What happens to %s next? Pick the machine:
scc.logic.route.broken: This step does not use %s - the route is broken here
scc.logic.route.chosen: This recipe is used for this step
scc.logic.route.click: Click to change or remove this step
scc.logic.route.empty: No items yet - add the items whose recipe you want to fix.
scc.logic.route.end.tip: End of the route - this is what the order makes
scc.logic.route.full: A route has at most %s steps.
scc.logic.route.intro: Build the exact path: pick the raw material, then add machine after machine. Orders through this route go exactly this way - before the network rules and your own recipe choices.
scc.logic.route.next.tip: Add the next machine to the route
scc.logic.route.nocats: No machine categories - the network needs a terminal and machines.
scc.logic.route.noruns: No machine for this in the network
scc.logic.route.nostart: Choose the raw material first - click the first field of the route.
scc.logic.route.own.hint: Click a slot to choose an item, scroll to change the amount (Shift: 8), right-click to clear. The machine does the real work - SCC only plans with your numbers.
scc.logic.route.recipe.none: The recipe catalogue knows no recipe for this item - use an own recipe.
scc.logic.route.runs: A machine for this is in the network
scc.logic.route.slot.tip: Click: choose item - scroll: amount (Shift: 8) - right-click: clear
scc.logic.route.start.hint: Where does the route begin? For example Raw Iron. After that you add the machines one by one - each step shows only recipes that really use the item before it.
scc.logic.route.start.tip: Click to change the raw material
scc.logic.route.title: Recipe route
scc.logic.rsmode.level.tip: The value itself is the signal strength (0-15) - for fill-level lamp chains.
scc.logic.rsmode.switch.tip: Any value except 0 gives full strength 15 - like a lever.
scc.logic.status.empty: Empty plan - start with a template or drag nodes from the palette
scc.logic.tpl.insert.tip: Insert at a free spot next to your plan (double-click or Enter works too)
scc.logic.tpl.inserted: Template inserted: %s - click a node to adjust it
scc.logic.tpl.iron_alarm.desc: Below 1000 Iron Ingots, the plan orders iron along YOUR recipe route (with Mekanism: Enrichment Chamber 3 Raw Iron -> 4 Iron Dust, then the furnace; otherwise the Blast Furnace). While it produces, a Blinker flashes the redstone output - put a lamp next to the block.
scc.logic.tpl.iron_alarm.note: Iron below 1000: produce it along my route (left). While the order runs, the lamp next to this block blinks. Adjust the route via 'Edit route...'.
scc.logic.tpl.keep_stock.desc: Below the target (1000 Iron Ingots), the network orders what is missing - with the normal recipe of your network. The display shows the stock live. Pick your own item in the Stock and Order nodes.
scc.logic.tpl.keep_stock.note: Keeps 1000 Iron Ingots in stock. Change the item in 'Stock' and 'Order', the amount in 'Compare' and 'Order'.
scc.logic.tpl.keep_stock.short: Never run out of an item
scc.logic.tpl.night_shift.desc: Only at night the plan keeps 4096 Stone Bricks in stock, in batches of 512 - your machines work while you sleep and stay free for you during the day. Change the item for your own building project.
scc.logic.tpl.night_shift.note: At night: fill Stone Bricks up to 4096 in batches of 512. During the day the machines stay free for you.
scc.logic.tpl.overflow.desc: Above 10,000 Cobblestone, a message appears above your hotbar (at most every 5 minutes) and the redstone output switches on - e.g. a warning lamp or a Toggle Bus that stops the quarry.
scc.logic.tpl.overflow.note: Warns when more than 10,000 Cobblestone pile up: message + redstone. The message waits 5 minutes before it repeats.
scc.logic.tpl.power_saver.desc: Below 20 % power the redstone output switches on and stays on until power is back above 50 % (the Latch remembers it). Put a Toggle Bus next to the block to cut off less important parts of your network.
scc.logic.tpl.power_saver.note: Power below 20 %: redstone on (e.g. Toggle Bus cuts off a part of the network). Only above 50 % it switches off again - no flickering.
scc.logic.tpl.storage_display.desc: The stock becomes a redstone strength: every 1000 Cobblestone add one level, up to 15 at 15,000. Lay redstone dust with lamps from the block - the further the light reaches, the fuller your storage. At 15,000 a short message tells you it is full.
scc.logic.tpl.storage_display.note: Cobblestone as a lamp chain: 1 level per 1000, at most 15. Display shows the exact number; at 15,000 a message says it is full.
scc.logic.tpl.storage_display.short: Fill level as a lamp chain
scc.logic.tpl.title: Templates - pick one to see what it does
scc.logic.what.fill.tip: How full the machine's slots are, 0-100 %.
scc.logic.what.full.tip: 1 when every slot of the machine is full - it cannot take more.
scc.logic.what.idle.tip: 1 while no order uses the calculator and its machine shows no work.
scc.lognet.stale_link: This wrench was still linked to %s at %s, %s, %s, but there is no storage controller there anymore. The old link was removed - this controller is linked now.
scc.machine.status.full: Machine does not take the ingredients (slots occupied)
scc.machine.status.handonly: Works by hand only - no inventory
scc.machine.status.idle: Idle - free for the next order
scc.machine.status.nofuel: Stopped: the furnace has no fuel
scc.machine.status.turn: Waiting for its turn (shared with other orders)
scc.meteor.burned: A meteor burned up in the sky.
scc.meteor.caught: A Sky Harvester caught a meteor!
scc.meteorite.tip: Fell from the sky. Mine it for ores and Star Shards.
scc.module.armor_breaker.desc: 25% of the target's armor per level counts for nothing. 50 FE per hit.
scc.module.clarity.desc: Blindness and Darkness vanish at once. 100 FE each time.
scc.module.critical.desc: 15% chance per level for a critical hit without jumping. 50 FE per extra crit.
scc.module.detox.desc: Poison, Wither and Weakness vanish. 150 FE per effect.
scc.module.efficiency.desc: Mines faster like the enchantment. 10 FE per block and level.
scc.module.fortune.desc: Fortune at the module level - beyond III up to the Apothic Enchanting maximum. Rests while the drill is set to Silk Touch.
scc.module.jump.desc: Jump higher and fall 2 blocks per level softer. 20 FE per jump and level.
scc.module.light.desc: In the dark the drill places an invisible starlight (light level 13) at your feet. 200 FE per light.
scc.module.looting.desc: Looting at the module level (up to the Apothic Enchanting maximum, otherwise III). The tier bonus (+1) stacks on top.
scc.module.power.desc: Plasma arrows hit 20% harder per level. 20 FE per arrow and level.
scc.module.quick.none: No modules in worn or held Stellar Gear.
scc.module.quick.title: Modules
scc.module.quick_draw.desc: Fully drawn 3 ticks sooner per level (at least 5 ticks).
scc.module.regeneration.desc: The Regeneration effect at the module's level (I-IV), with its icon in the HUD. 60 FE/s per level, only while you are hurt.
scc.module.sharpness.desc: +2.5 damage per level (also for the Plasma Sickle). 25 FE per hit and level.
scc.module.speed.desc: +15% walking speed per level. 10 FE/s per level.
scc.module.star_sight.desc: Ores (gold) and mobs (red = hostile) glow through walls - only you see it. Range 8/16/24 blocks, 20 FE/s per level.
scc.module.star_sight.effect: ores and mobs glow within %s blocks
scc.module.step_assist.desc: Walk up full blocks without jumping (not while sneaking). 5 FE/s.
scc.module.tip.how: Install: sneak + right-click the gear, then "Modules".
scc.module.tip.max: Up to level %s (higher tiers allow more)
scc.module.tip.stack: Each module is one level - install three for level III.
scc.module.trash_filter.desc: Cobblestone, dirt, netherrack, gravel and stone variants vanish instead of dropping (tag scc:stellar_trash).
scc.module.ui.button.tip: Open the module window of this piece.
scc.module.ui.click.inv: Click: install one level from your inventory
scc.module.ui.click.net: Click: install one level from the linked network
scc.module.ui.empty.tip: Install a module from the list on the left.
scc.module.ui.level.more: Install more modules for this level.
scc.module.ui.load.free.tip: %s core load free for more modules or higher levels.
scc.module.ui.load.tip: Every active module level costs core load. This piece carries %s and has %s slots - choose what matters.
scc.module.ui.load.title: Core load
scc.module.ui.next.off: Costs %s core load, only %s free - it is installed switched off
scc.module.ui.none: You have none - forge it in the Star Forge.
scc.module.ui.nothing: No modules yet. Click a module on the left to install it - each one is a level.
scc.module.ui.remove.tip: The module goes back into your inventory.
scc.module.ui.title: Stellar Modules
scc.module.vitality.desc: +2 hearts per level (up to +10). 20 FE/s per level.
scc.module.water_breathing.desc: Your air never runs out under water. 40 FE per second submerged.
scc.module.water_walk.desc: Walk on water like on solid ground. Sneak to dive in. 40 FE/s on water.
scc.module.why.fits: This module does not fit here.
scc.module.why.max: This module is already at its highest level.
scc.module.why.slots: All slots are taken - a higher tier opens more.
scc.module.why.tier: This tier cannot hold a higher level - upgrade the piece in the Star Anvil.

scc.obs.why.blocked.output: Results had nowhere to go - storage full. %s machine(s). Add storage or free some space.
scc.obs.why.blocked.power: %s machine(s) were switched off by the controller (load shedding) or the network ran out of power.
scc.obs.why.busy: Bottleneck: %s machine(s) of this type were almost always working. Orders waited %s%% of their time for one.
scc.obs.why.busy.free: %s machine(s) of this type were almost always working, but no order had to wait for one yet. If more orders come, this is the next bottleneck.
scc.obs.why.deficit: On average %s FE/t came in and %s FE/t went out; storage is %s%% full. Add generation before it runs empty.
scc.obs.why.idle: %s machine(s) of this type had nothing to do in this time window - free for other work.
scc.obs.why.jobsmissing: Raw materials or intermediate products ran short. The order details show what is missing - keep it in stock with standing orders.
scc.obs.why.missing: Orders reached this machine before their ingredients. Keep the intermediate products in stock (standing orders) or speed up their supply.
scc.obs.why.nofuel: Keep fuel in storage - Processing Calculators refuel furnaces from the network.
scc.obs.why.nomachine: Some steps found no machine in the network that can do them. The order details show which machine is missing.
scc.obs.why.offline: The controller had no energy, so nothing worked. Add generation or energy storage.
scc.obs.why.queue: More orders than may run at once. Allow more parallel orders in the controller rules, or add Calculation Crafters and machines.
scc.obs.why.storagefull: Share of order time with nowhere to put results. Add item or fluid storage, or clear some.

scc.star.notyours: This Little Star belongs to someone else.
scc.star_shard.tip: Found in meteorites. Nine make a Red Dwarf Ember.
scc.starlight.tip2: Eight of one kind + a dye: recolor them.
scc.starlog.bridge.hint: Join two places with a wireless transmitter and receiver.
scc.starlog.chain.hint: Order something that takes several recipes in a row.
scc.starlog.chronon.hint: Condensed time - ask a black hole.
scc.starlog.cradle.hint: Light a star in the Stellar Cradle.
scc.starlog.exo_flight.hint: Wear a full Singularity Stellar Exo set.
scc.starlog.footer: Kept by itself, book or not.
scc.starlog.forge.hint: Forge something in the Star Forge.
scc.starlog.gear.hint: Craft a piece of Stellar Gear.
scc.starlog.gear_blue_giant.hint: Raise a piece of Stellar Gear to Blue Giant.
scc.starlog.gear_neutron_star.hint: Raise a piece of Stellar Gear to Neutron Star.
scc.starlog.gear_red_dwarf.hint: Raise a piece of Stellar Gear to Red Dwarf.
scc.starlog.gear_singularity.hint: Raise a piece of Stellar Gear to Singularity.
scc.starlog.gear_yellow_star.hint: Raise a piece of Stellar Gear to Yellow Star.
scc.starlog.item.tip: Right-click: your milestones in SCC, with the day you reached each one.
scc.starlog.lens.hint: Make a lens for the Sky Harvester.
scc.starlog.little_star.hint: Hold a Little Star in your hands.
scc.starlog.matter_blue_giant.hint: A Blue Giant needs an even stronger lens.
scc.starlog.matter_neutron_star.hint: Only the best lenses reach a Neutron Star.
scc.starlog.matter_red_dwarf.hint: Harvest a Red Dwarf in the sky.
scc.starlog.matter_singularity.hint: The last thing the sky has to give.
scc.starlog.matter_yellow_star.hint: A better lens reaches a Yellow Star.
scc.starlog.meteor.hint: Be close when a Sky Harvester catches a falling meteor.
scc.starlog.meteor_shower.hint: Be in a world with sky objects when a meteor shower night begins (every new moon).
scc.starlog.network.hint: Power a Calculator Controller, attach storage and open a terminal.
scc.starlog.order.hint: Let the network craft something you do not have.
scc.starlog.pocket.hint: Hold a Stellar Pocket in your hands.
scc.starlog.pulsar.hint: Let a Blue Giant end its life in the Stellar Cradle - and keep the barrier up.
scc.starlog.quarry.hint: Let a Star Quarry finish its whole area.
scc.starlog.sky.hint: Let a Sky Harvester collect its first piece.
scc.starlog.sky_sensor.hint: Hold a Sky Sensor in your hands.

scc.starlog.stat.orders.hint: Autocrafting orders you placed that finished.
scc.starlog.stat.quarry.hint: Blocks your Star Quarries dug out - also while you were away.
scc.starlog.stat.showers.hint: Meteor shower nights you spent under the open sky.
scc.starlog.stat.stored.hint: Everything you put into a network yourself - terminal, wireless terminal, Store inventory.
scc.starlog.stat.wormhole.hint: Jumps through a Wormhole Gate or the rift of a Wormhole Remote.

scc.starlog.toast.head: Star Logbook
